title: Wind-driven fire
plain: On a grid, fire spreads each turn only east, north and south (the wind blocks westward spread). How few firefighters per turn can always trap a single burning cell?
math: On $\mathbb{Z}^2$, burning cells ignite neighbours at offsets $(1,0),(0,\pm1)$ each turn; $k$ unburnt cells are protected per turn. Find the least $k$ that always yields a finite burned set.

title: Beat the prism
plain: Gerver's sofa, lifted to one unit tall, can turn a corner in a square pipe. Find a 3D shape with more volume that can still make the turn.
math: In the corridor $([0,1]\times\mathbb{R}\cup\mathbb{R}\times[0,1])\times[0,1]$ turning about the $z$-axis, find a rigid motion-admissible solid of volume $>2.2195\ldots$.

title: Lonely runner with one fast runner
plain: Runners have speeds 1, 2, 3 and some larger speed m. Work out exactly how lonely a stationary runner is guaranteed to get, depending on m.
math: Compute $\delta(m)=\sup_t\min(\|t\|,\|2t\|,\|3t\|,\|mt\|)$ in closed form for all integers $m\ge4$.

title: Hardest Rush Hour
plain: Find the 7 × 7 Rush Hour traffic-jam puzzle that takes the most moves to solve.
math: Over all solvable $7\times7$ Rush Hour configurations, determine $\max$ of the minimum solution length, with a certificate.

title: Fewest burned cells
plain: In the wind-driven fire (spreading only east, north and south), with the fewest firefighters that can trap it, what is the least area that must burn?
math: For the minimal $k$ in the east/north/south fire on $\mathbb{Z}^2$, find $\min |B_\infty|$ over all protection strategies.

title: Infinite Prime Nim losses
plain: Prime Nim has infinitely many losing pile sizes (a known theorem, since primes have arbitrarily large gaps). Show they are rare.
math: Let $L=\{n: G(n)=0\}$ for the subtraction game with prime moves ($|L|=\infty$ is known). Prove $L$ has natural density $0$.

title: Lean golf is NP-hard
plain: Show that finding the shortest proof using only a few basic Lean tactics is computationally hard.
math: Prove NP-hardness of: given a Lean 4 goal and $k$ in unary, is there a proof using only intro, apply, exact, rfl with at most $k$ steps?

title: Obtuse sofa
plain: The corridor turns 120° instead of 90°. Find a sofa and a matching upper bound within 1%.
math: For a width-1 corridor with turn angle $2\pi/3$, find $A$ with an admissible sofa of area $A$ and a proof that the optimum is $<1.01A$.

title: Graceful spider forests
plain: Spiders are trees with one central branching vertex. Show forests of spiders have the distinct-difference labeling.
math: For any forest of spiders with $m$ edges and $c$ components, find a bijection $V\to\{0,\dots,m+c-1\}$ with distinct edge differences.

title: Smallest-odd-factor Collatz
plain: Halve even numbers; send an odd number to the smallest odd prime dividing 3n + 1. Find every cycle that occurs below a billion.
math: Let $g(n)=n/2$ ($n$ even) and $g(n)=q(3n+1)$ ($n$ odd), $q$ the least odd prime factor ($1$ if none). Classify all cycles of $g$ meeting $[1,10^9]$.

title: Narrowing doorway sofa
plain: A width-1 hallway turns a right angle and then narrows to width 0.8. Find the biggest sofa that gets through.
math: Maximize the area of a connected planar set movable from arm $\mathbb{R}_{<0}\times[0,1]$ into arm $[0,0.8]\times\mathbb{R}_{>1}$.

title: Shuffle with a cut
plain: Do a perfect shuffle, then cut k cards from top to bottom, and repeat. How many repetitions bring the deck back?
math: For the permutation $c_k\circ\sigma_{\text{out}}$ on $2n$ cards, determine its order as a function of $n$ and $k$.

title: Anti-knight Sudoku
plain: In this Sudoku, equal digits may not sit a knight's move apart. What is the fewest clues for a unique solution?
math: Determine the minimum number of givens in a uniquely solvable $9\times9$ Sudoku with the extra anti-knight constraint.

title: Sofa angle monotonicity
plain: As a hallway's turn gets sharper, the best sofa should get smaller. Prove it between 60° and 90°.
math: Let $A(\theta)$ be the maximal sofa area for a width-1 corridor turning by $\theta$. Prove $A$ is decreasing on $[\pi/3,\pi/2]$.

title: Delayed firefighters
plain: Fire spreads in four directions, but a firefighter assigned now only takes effect a turn later. How many per turn are needed?
math: On $\mathbb{Z}^2$ with 4-neighbour spread, cells chosen at turn $t$ become protected at turn $t+1$. Find the least per-turn number that contains a single fire.

title: Aperiodic polykite census
plain: The "hat" is made of 8 kites and tiles the plane only non-periodically. Find every such shape made of at most 12 kites.
math: Enumerate all polykites with $\le12$ kites (from the $\{6,3\}$ kite grid) that tile $\mathbb{R}^2$ but admit no periodic tiling.

title: Fire on a cylinder
plain: A fire burns on a grid wrapped into an infinite tube of width n. How many firefighters per turn stop it?
math: On $C_n\times\mathbb{Z}$ with 4-neighbour spread, find the least $k(n)$ that always contains a single fire, for every $n$.

title: Mod-3 Collatz map
plain: Divide by 3 when you can; otherwise double and add or subtract 1. Find all loops below a billion.
math: Let $h(n)=n/3$ if $3\mid n$, $2n+1$ if $n\equiv1$, $2n-1$ if $n\equiv2 \pmod 3$. Classify all cycles of $h$ meeting $[1,10^9]$.

title: Voice leading is NP-hard
plain: Moving n voices through a chord progression with the least total motion while avoiding parallel fifths should be computationally hard.
math: Show NP-hardness of minimizing $\sum_t\sum_i |x_{t+1,i}-x_{t,i}|$ over voicings of a given chord sequence with $n$ voices, subject to no parallel perfect fifths.

title: Real-rank hyperoperations
plain: Addition, multiplication and exponentiation are ranks 1, 2, 3 of one ladder. Find natural rules that fix a unique operation at every real rank in between.
math: Find axioms (analytic in $s$, $a[s{+}1](b{+}1)=a[s](a[s{+}1]b)$, agreement with $+,\times,\uparrow$ at $s=1,2,3$) that determine $a[s]b$ uniquely for real $s\in[1,3]$, and prove uniqueness.

title: Adversarial 2048
plain: An opponent places every new tile in 2048 as unhelpfully as possible. What is the biggest tile you can still guarantee?
math: On the $4\times4$ board where an adversary chooses each spawn's position and value in $\{2,4\}$, determine the largest tile the player can force.

title: Blank jigsaw
plain: A jigsaw with no picture can only be solved from piece shapes. How few edge shapes force a unique solution?
math: Find the asymptotics in $n$ of the least number of edge types such that some $n\times n$ jigsaw has exactly one assembly (up to rotation of the whole).

title: Quarter-tone all-interval rows
plain: Count the tone rows in 24-note tuning that use every interval exactly once.
math: Count permutations of $\mathbb{Z}_{24}$ whose successive differences are all distinct nonzero residues, and find their growth rate for $\mathbb{Z}_{2m}$.

title: Small Keller maps in 3D
plain: The 2026 counterexamples to the Jacobian conjecture have fairly high degree. Is there one of degree 5 or less?
math: Decide whether some $F:\mathbb{C}^3\to\mathbb{C}^3$ with $\deg F\le5$ and $\det DF\in\mathbb{C}^\times$ has no polynomial inverse.

title: Prime Nim, misère
plain: In Prime Nim where the last mover loses instead of wins, do the losing positions differ from normal play only finitely often?
math: Compare the P-positions of the prime subtraction game in normal and misère play; decide whether their symmetric difference is finite.

title: Seven-free Egyptian fractions
plain: Write every fraction as a sum of distinct unit fractions whose denominators never contain the digit 7.
math: Prove every $q\in\mathbb{Q}\cap(0,1)$ is $\sum_{d\in D}1/d$ for a finite set $D$ of distinct integers with no decimal digit 7.

title: Hyperbolic sofa, flat limit
plain: As curvature fades to zero, the best hyperbolic sofa should approach Gerver's sofa. Find how fast.
math: Let $A(\kappa)$ be the optimal sofa area in curvature $-\kappa$. Prove $A(\kappa)=2.2195\ldots+c\kappa+o(\kappa)$ and compute $c$.

title: Penrose firefighter
plain: Fire spreads along a Penrose tiling's edges. How many firefighters per turn can trap any fire?
math: On the vertex graph of a Penrose rhomb tiling, find the least $k$ such that protecting $k$ vertices per turn contains a fire from any single vertex.

title: Three-pile shuffle group
plain: Using the six ways to stack three piles in a perfect shuffle, which rearrangements of the deck can you reach?
math: Determine the subgroup of $S_{3n}$ generated by the six 3-pile perfect shuffles (all pile orders), for every $n$.

title: Two-tree graceful forests
plain: Check the distinct-difference labeling for every forest of two small trees.
math: Prove that every forest of two trees with at most 25 vertices each has a bijection $V\to\{0,\dots,m+1\}$ with distinct edge differences.

title: Shortest proof that √2 is irrational
plain: Find the shortest possible Lean proof that the square root of 2 is irrational, and prove nothing shorter works.
math: Over Lean 4 core tactics on top of Mathlib's definitions, find the minimal tactic-step proof of `Irrational (Real.sqrt 2)` and certify minimality.

title: Pipe-bend sofa
plain: A round pipe of diameter 1 bends at a right angle. What is the biggest solid that fits around the bend?
math: Maximize volume over rigid-motion-admissible solids in the union of two half-cylinders of diameter 1 meeting at a right angle.

title: Counting 16 × 16 Sudoku
plain: Count the essentially different 16 × 16 Sudoku grids, ignoring symmetries, to three significant figures.
math: Determine the automorphism group $\Gamma$ of the $16\times16$ Sudoku constraint structure and estimate $|\text{grids}/\Gamma|$ to 3 significant figures.

title: Toroidal Hex
plain: Hex on a doughnut: the board wraps around, and you win with a chain that loops the long way. Who wins on 7 × 7?
math: On the $7\times7$ Hex board with opposite sides identified, a player wins with a non-contractible chain of their colour; determine the winner and whether draws occur.

title: Hyperbolic firefighter budgets
plain: In a hyperbolic tiling, fire spreads exponentially, so no fixed crew stops it. How fast must the crew grow?
math: On the $\{7,3\}$ tiling graph, find the minimal growth of budgets $k_t$ (firefighters at turn $t$) that contains any single fire.

title: Kissing hats
plain: How many copies of the hat tile can touch one hat without overlapping?
math: Determine the maximum number of interior-disjoint congruent copies of the hat polykite, reflections allowed, each meeting a fixed hat.

title: Packing seven-pointed stars
plain: Find the densest way to pack identical seven-pointed stars in the plane.
math: Determine the maximal packing density of congruent copies of the regular star polygon $\{7/2\}$.

title: Square in a snowflake
plain: Find the largest square whose four corners lie on the Koch snowflake.
math: Prove the Koch snowflake inscribes a square, and determine the maximal side length of an inscribed square.

title: Formalize 3D Kakeya
plain: Turn the 2025 proof of the three-dimensional Kakeya conjecture into a compact computer-checked proof.
math: Produce a Lean 4 formalization of the Wang–Zahl theorem ($\dim_H K=3$ for Kakeya $K\subset\mathbb{R}^3$) in under 50,000 lines beyond Mathlib.

title: Formalize the sofa
plain: Turn Baek's proof that Gerver's sofa is optimal into a computer-checked proof.
math: Formalize in Lean 4 the statement and proof that the moving sofa constant equals the area of Gerver's sofa.

title: Hat patch complexity
plain: Count the distinct round patches of radius r in hat tilings. Find the exact constant in their growth.
math: Let $P(r)$ count radius-$r$ patches over the hat tiling hull. Prove $P(r)\sim C r^2$ and compute $C$.

title: Random walk on the hat tiling
plain: A random walker steps between neighbouring hat tiles. How likely is it to be back home after n steps?
math: For simple random walk on the hat adjacency graph, prove $p_{2n}(o,o)\sim c/n$ and compute $c$.

title: Percolation on the hat tiling
plain: Each hat tile is open at random with probability p. Find where an infinite open cluster first appears.
math: For site percolation on the hat adjacency graph, prove $0.6<p_c<0.7$ (or the correct interval) with rigorous bounds.

title: Self-avoiding walks on the hat tiling
plain: Count paths across hat tiles that never revisit a tile, and show their growth rate is new.
math: Prove the connective constant $\mu_{\text{hat}}$ exists for the hat adjacency graph and $\mu_{\text{hat}}\ne\sqrt{2+\sqrt2}$.

title: Independent prime-gap formalization
plain: Check the 2026 record that prime gaps of at most 186 occur forever, with a fresh computer proof written independently.
math: Give an independent Lean 4 proof of $\liminf_{n}(p_{n+1}-p_n)\le186$.

title: Optimal origami base
plain: Folders design animal shapes by packing circles on paper. Find the smallest paper needed for every stick figure with six legs or fewer.
math: For every weighted tree with $\le6$ leaves, determine the minimum square side admitting a uniaxial base (optimal circle–river packing), with certificates.

title: Keller maps with few terms
plain: Find a Jacobian-conjecture counterexample using as few polynomial terms as possible.
math: Minimize the total number of monomials of $F:\mathbb{C}^3\to\mathbb{C}^3$ with $\det DF\in\mathbb{C}^\times$ and $F$ not injective; prove minimality.

title: Billiards in the sofa
plain: A ball bounces inside Gerver's sofa shape. Find its shortest closed bouncing path.
math: Determine the minimal-length periodic billiard trajectory in Gerver's sofa and prove minimality.

title: Fewest KenKen cages
plain: What is the fewest cages for a uniquely solvable 6 × 6 KenKen puzzle?
math: Minimize the number of cages in a $6\times6$ KenKen (cage targets with $+,-,\times,\div$) having a unique Latin-square solution.

title: S and Z Tetris
plain: If only the S and Z pieces ever come, how many lines can you clear before losing on a 10-wide board?
math: On a $10\times20$ Tetris well with an adversarial sequence from $\{S,Z\}$, determine the maximum number of lines the player can guarantee.

title: The 2048 ceiling
plain: Show that even perfect play almost never reaches the theoretical top tile in 2048.
math: Prove $\Pr(\text{reach }131072)<10^{-6}$ for every strategy on the $4\times4$ board with standard random spawns.

title: Equal-area triangles in the hat
plain: Cut the hat tile into triangles of equal area. Which numbers of triangles are possible?
math: Determine the set of $n$ for which the hat polygon admits a dissection into $n$ triangles of equal area.

title: Fire on the Sierpinski graph
plain: With one firefighter per turn on the Sierpinski triangle graph, what fraction must burn as the graph gets bigger?
math: On the level-$n$ Sierpinski gasket graph with a fire at a corner and one protected vertex per turn, find $\lim_n \min |B|/|V|$.

title: Prime squared square
plain: Tile a square with smaller squares, all different sizes, every side a prime number. Find one or show none exists.
math: Find a perfect squared square whose component squares all have prime side lengths, or prove none exists.

title: Integer sofa
plain: With the hallway scaled to width 10, what is the biggest polygon with whole-number corners that turns the corner?
math: Maximize area over lattice polygons admissible in the width-10 right-angled corridor.

title: Polyhedral sofa
plain: The best 3D sofa is curved. What is the best one with at most 12 flat corners?
math: Maximize volume over convex polyhedra with $\le12$ vertices admissible in the $1\times1$ square corridor.

title: Toroidal Sudoku
plain: Sudoku where the 3 × 3 boxes wrap around the board's edges. What is the fewest clues for a unique solution?
math: For the $9\times9$ Sudoku variant whose box regions are a fixed partition into wrapped $3\times3$ blocks on $\mathbb{Z}_9^2$, find the minimum number of givens.

title: Five colors for square sums
plain: Square-sum graphs need four colors eventually. Do they eventually need five?
math: Decide whether $\chi(S_N)\ge5$ for all sufficiently large $N$.

title: Hamiltonian induced subgraphs of S_N
plain: Show deciding whether a given set of numbers can be lined up so neighbours sum to squares is NP-complete.
math: Prove NP-completeness of: given $A\subset\mathbb{N}$ (in binary), decide whether $S_\infty[A]$ has a Hamiltonian path.

title: Monotile assembly threshold
plain: With one tile shape, deciding whether a region can be tiled is easy in some cases; with many shapes it is hard. Find the smallest number of shapes where it becomes hard.
math: Find the least $t$ such that some fixed set of $t$ polygons makes "does this finite region admit an exact tiling?" NP-complete, and prove all sets of fewer polygons give polynomial-time problems.

title: Square-sum coloring
plain: Join numbers that add up to a perfect square. Does the number of colors needed stay bounded forever?
math: Decide whether $\sup_N \chi(S_N)<\infty$.

title: Hyperbolic sofa
plain: Find the largest sofa that can turn a right-angled corner in a hallway of width 1 in the hyperbolic plane, and prove it is best.
math: Determine $\sup\{\operatorname{area}(S)\}$ over sets $S\subset\mathbb{H}^2$ admissible in the width-1 right-angled corridor, and an optimizer.

title: Hyperbolic square peg
plain: Every closed curve in the hyperbolic plane should pass through the corners of some hyperbolic square.
math: Prove every Jordan curve in $\mathbb{H}^2$ contains the four vertices of a regular hyperbolic quadrilateral.

title: FLT, compressed
plain: Fermat's Last Theorem has a huge computer formalization effort. Do it in far fewer lines.
math: Give a Lean 4 proof of $x^n+y^n=z^n\Rightarrow xyz=0$ for $n\ge3$ using at most $10^5$ lines beyond current Mathlib.

title: Prime pancakes
plain: Sort pancakes by flipping only a prime number at a time. Find the worst-case number of flips asymptotically.
math: With prefix reversals of prime length, determine $\lim_n d(n)/n$ for the worst-case sorting distance $d(n)$.

title: Seven-free three primes
plain: Every large odd number should be a sum of three primes that never use the digit 7.
math: Prove every sufficiently large odd $N$ is $p_1+p_2+p_3$ with each $p_i$ prime and free of the decimal digit 7.

title: Spherical sofa
plain: Find the biggest shape that turns a right-angled corner in a width-1 hallway drawn on a large sphere.
math: On the sphere of radius 10, determine the maximal area of a set admissible in the width-1 right-angled geodesic corridor.

title: No prism sofa
plain: Show the best 3D sofa is genuinely three-dimensional, not just a flat shape extruded upward.
math: Prove no optimal solid for the $1\times1$ square corridor is of the form $A\times[0,1]$.

title: Blokus Duo
plain: Who wins two-player Blokus with perfect play?
math: Weakly solve Blokus Duo on the $14\times14$ board with standard starting points.

title: Square-sum cliques
plain: How many numbers can pairwise add up to perfect squares? Decide if there is a limit.
math: Decide whether $\omega(S_N)$ is bounded, i.e., whether there exist arbitrarily large sets of distinct positive integers with all pairwise sums square.

title: Square-sum spectral gap
plain: Find how well connected the square-sum graph is, through its eigenvalues.
math: Determine the asymptotics of $\lambda_1(S_N)-\lambda_2(S_N)$ for the adjacency spectrum.

title: Seven-free primes in progressions
plain: Primes avoiding the digit 7 should be evenly spread among remainder classes.
math: Prove primes without decimal digit 7 are equidistributed in residue classes mod $q$ for all $q\le(\log x)^A$.

title: Largest-factor Collatz heights
plain: For almost every start, the largest-factor Collatz orbit never climbs past a fixed power of where it started.
math: Prove there is $C$ with $\max_k f^k(n)\le n^C$ for a density-1 set of $n$.

title: Coloring the spectre's distances
plain: Take all corners of a spectre tiling and join two whenever they are exactly one edge-length apart. How many colors are needed?
math: Determine the chromatic number of the unit-distance graph on the vertex set of a spectre tiling (unit = edge length).

title: Isospectral polykites
plain: Two different drums can sound the same. Find two different shapes made of kites that do.
math: Find two non-congruent polykites whose Dirichlet Laplacians have identical spectra.

title: Distant-force blow-up
plain: The 2026 Navier–Stokes blow-up pushed fluid right where it broke. Make it break with a push kept far away.
math: Construct smooth compactly supported $f$ with $\operatorname{supp} f\cap B(x_*,1)=\emptyset$ such that 3D Navier–Stokes from rest blows up at $x_*$ in finite time.

title: Closed-form Euler blow-up
plain: Give smooth starting data for frictionless 3D fluid, written as an explicit formula, that blows up.
math: Find closed-form smooth finite-energy $u_0$ on $\mathbb{R}^3$ whose unforced Euler solution blows up in finite time.

title: Tangent-sweep Keller maps
plain: One 2026 counterexample to the Jacobian conjecture sweeps tangent lines of a curve. Find every counterexample built that way.
math: Classify all polynomial maps $\mathbb{C}^3\to\mathbb{C}^3$ with constant nonzero Jacobian arising from the tangent-sweep construction over plane curves.

title: Two-to-one Keller maps
plain: Known Jacobian counterexamples cover most points three or more times. Is there one covering most points exactly twice?
math: Decide whether some $F:\mathbb{C}^3\to\mathbb{C}^3$ with $\det DF\in\mathbb{C}^\times$ has generic fiber size exactly 2.

title: Two fires
plain: Two fires start a distance d apart. How many firefighters per turn are needed, depending on d?
math: On $\mathbb{Z}^2$ with 4-neighbour spread, find the least $k(d)$ containing fires started at $(0,0)$ and $(d,0)$.

title: Building a firebreak
plain: Firefighters must build one connected wall, one cell per turn, each next to the last. Can they ever enclose the fire?
math: On $\mathbb{Z}^2$, each turn add one protected cell 8-adjacent to the previous one. Decide whether a single fire can be enclosed, and for which build rates.

title: Hex on hats
plain: Play Hex on a board made of hat tiles. Can games end in a draw, and who wins on a small board?
math: For Hex on hat-tiled rhombus boards, decide whether draws are possible, and solve side length 5.

title: Go on a torus
plain: Go on a 7 × 7 board that wraps around. What komi makes the game fair?
math: Determine the perfect-play score of Go on $\mathbb{Z}_7^2$ (area scoring, positional superko).

title: Worst-case Battleship
plain: What is the fewest shots that always sinks the standard fleet on a 10 × 10 board?
math: Compute the minimax number of shots to sink ships of lengths 5,4,3,3,2 on $10\times10$ against an adversary who may move ships consistently with past answers.

title: Benford orbits
plain: The leading digits of largest-factor Collatz orbits should follow Benford's law.
math: Prove that for almost all $n$ the leading digits of $(f^k(n))_{k\le T(n)}$ satisfy Benford's law as $n\to\infty$.

title: Random graceful forests
plain: Almost every random forest has the distinct-edge-difference labeling.
math: For a uniform random forest with $m$ edges and $c\sim\alpha m$ components, prove the graceful-forest labeling exists with probability $\to1$.

title: T-junction sofa
plain: A sofa comes up the stem of a T and must be able to leave by either arm. Find the biggest one.
math: Maximize area over sets admissible from the stem to each arm (separately) of a width-1 T-junction.

title: Car-like sofa
plain: The sofa moves like a car: forward only, with limited steering. Find the biggest that makes the corner.
math: Maximize area over shapes whose motion is a forward Dubins path with turning radius $\ge1$ through the width-1 right-angled corridor.

title: Fire on a random planet
plain: Fire spreads on a random planar map. Find how fast firefighting budgets must grow.
math: On the uniform infinite planar triangulation, determine the minimal growth exponent $a$ such that budgets $k_t=t^{a}$ contain a fire almost surely.

title: Random lonely runners
plain: With random speeds, runners get noticeably lonelier than the conjecture promises.
math: For i.i.d. uniform speeds in $[1,N]$, $N\gg n^3$, prove the loneliness gap exceeds $\frac1{n+1}+c\frac{\log n}{n^2}$ with probability $\to1$.

title: Sudoku resolution bounds
plain: Proving a large broken Sudoku has no solution should require long logical proofs.
math: Prove resolution refutations of unsatisfiable $n^2\times n^2$ Sudoku instances require size $2^{n^{\Omega(1)}}$ for some explicit family.

title: Quoridor
plain: Who wins the board game Quoridor with perfect play?
math: Weakly solve two-player Quoridor on the $9\times9$ board with 10 walls each.

title: Prime-frequency synchrony
plain: Oscillators with frequencies set by logarithms of primes eventually synchronize when coupled strongly enough. Find the threshold.
math: For the Kuramoto model with $\omega_i=\log p_i$, prove a sharp synchronization threshold $K_c(N)$ and its asymptotics.

title: Hat billiard counting
plain: Count the periodic bouncing paths inside a hat-shaped table up to a given length.
math: For billiards in the hat polygon, prove $N(L)\sim cL^2$ for periodic cylinder families and compute $c$.

title: Kakeya for hats
plain: What is the smallest region in which you can rotate a hat tile through every orientation?
math: Determine $\inf$ area of sets containing a translate of every rotation of the hat polygon.

title: BB(5), compressed
plain: The Busy Beaver value BB(5) was proved with a large computer proof. Make it small.
math: Prove $BB(5)=47{,}176{,}870$ in Lean 4 in under 10,000 lines.

title: Four colors, compressed
plain: Make the computer-checked four color theorem much shorter.
math: Give a Lean 4 proof of the four color theorem in under 20,000 lines beyond Mathlib.

title: Kepler, compressed
plain: Make the computer-checked proof of the densest sphere packing far shorter.
math: Give a Lean 4 proof of the Kepler conjecture in under 100,000 lines.

title: Fast Prime Nim
plain: Compute Prime Nim values up to a trillion.
math: Give an algorithm computing $G(n)$ for all $n\le10^{12}$ in time $o(N^{1.5})$ and run it.

title: Hat electrons
plain: An electron hopping on a hat tiling should have an unusual, fractal energy spectrum.
math: Prove the tight-binding Hamiltonian on the hat adjacency graph has purely singular continuous spectrum on a set of full measure in the hull.

title: Hat dimers
plain: Cover a hat tiling with dominoes joining neighbouring tiles. Count the coverings exactly per tile.
math: Compute the dimer entropy per vertex of the hat adjacency graph in closed form.

title: Emirps, almost
plain: Show infinitely many primes have a reversal with at most three prime factors.
math: Prove $\#\{p\le x: \Omega(\operatorname{rev}(p))\le3\}\to\infty$.

title: Smallest-factor Collatz, almost always
plain: For the smallest-odd-factor Collatz map, almost every start reaches 1.
math: Prove $g^k(n)=1$ for some $k$, for a density-1 set of $n$.

title: Hat random walk diffusivity
plain: A random walk across hat tiles should look like ordinary Brownian motion from far away. Find its exact spreading rate.
math: Prove the simple random walk on the hat adjacency graph satisfies an invariance principle with isotropic covariance $\sigma^2 I$, and compute $\sigma^2$.

title: Shuffle-sorting
plain: Using any of the six 3-pile perfect shuffles each time, how many shuffles reach any reachable arrangement in the worst case?
math: Determine the diameter of the Cayley graph of the 3-pile shuffle group on $3n$ cards, asymptotically in $n$.

title: A four-dimensional einstein
plain: Find one 4D shape that fills 4D space but only without repeating.
math: Find a connected tile $T\subset\mathbb{R}^4$ that tiles $\mathbb{R}^4$ by isometries but admits no periodic tiling.

title: Hinged sofa
plain: A sofa made of two rigid halves joined by a hinge. What total area can turn the corner?
math: Maximize $|A|+|B|$ for planar sets $A,B$ joined at a common point, moving with relative rotation allowed, through the width-1 right-angled corridor.

title: Firefighters on the front line
plain: Firefighters may only protect cells touching the fire. How many per turn are needed now?
math: On $\mathbb{Z}^2$ with protected cells required to be 4-adjacent to the burned set, find the least per-turn number containing a single fire.

title: Fire on a random tree
plain: On a tree where each node has three branches, fire jumps to two random branches per step. Can one firefighter per turn win?
math: On the 3-ary tree with fire spreading to a uniform random 2 of 3 children each step, compute $\Pr(\text{containment})$ with one protection per turn.

title: Sudoku transversals
plain: In every completed big Sudoku, find a set of cells with one in each row, each column and each symbol.
math: Prove every $n^2\times n^2$ Sudoku grid, viewed as a Latin square, has a transversal.

title: Effective Riemann constants
plain: Extract explicit, usable prime-counting error bounds from the 2026 Riemann proof.
math: From the 2026 Lean proof, extract and formally verify $|\pi(x)-\operatorname{li}(x)|\le\frac{1}{8\pi}\sqrt{x}\log x$ for all $x\ge2657$.

title: The sofa's boundary is not algebraic
plain: Gerver's sofa is bounded by 18 curve pieces. Show some of them are not polynomial curves.
math: Prove at least one boundary arc of Gerver's sofa is not contained in any algebraic curve.

title: Random Wang tiles
plain: Pick n random tile types with colored edges. How likely are they to tile the plane?
math: For $n$ Wang tiles with edge colours i.i.d. uniform in $[c]$, find the asymptotics of $\Pr(\text{tiles }\mathbb{Z}^2)$ as $n\to\infty$.

title: Random polykites
plain: Show almost no shapes made of many kites can tile the plane.
math: Prove the fraction of $k$-kite polykites that tile $\mathbb{R}^2$ decays exponentially in $k$.

title: Leaky firefighting
plain: Fire spreads to each neighbour only with probability p. Find the largest p at which one firefighter per turn wins.
math: On $\mathbb{Z}^2$ with each burning–unburnt edge transmitting independently with probability $p$, find $p^*$ such that one protection per turn contains the fire a.s. iff $p<p^*$.

title: Hat isoperimetry
plain: Among groups of n hat tiles, how short can the boundary be? Find the exact constant.
math: For the hat adjacency graph, prove $\min_{|A|=n}|\partial A|\sim c\sqrt n$ and compute $c$.

title: Undecidable polykite tiling
plain: For sets of five shapes made of kites, deciding whether they tile the plane is unsolvable by any algorithm.
math: Prove that tileability of $\mathbb{R}^2$ by finite sets of at most 5 polykites is undecidable.

title: Petersen Ramsey multiplicity
plain: In any two-coloring of a huge complete graph, how many single-color copies of the Petersen graph must appear, at least?
math: Determine the Ramsey multiplicity constant $\lim_n \min_{\text{2-col}} \#\text{mono } P / \#P \text{ in } K_n$ for the Petersen graph $P$.

title: Fire whirls
plain: Show the equations of buoyant flow allow a rotating column of fire that travels steadily.
math: Prove existence of a smooth traveling swirling solution of the 3D Boussinesq equations with a localized heat source.

title: Spot fires
plain: Fires throw embers ahead at random. Find the exact spreading speed.
math: For a growth model where each burning site ignites a site at i.i.d. heavy-tailed displacement at rate 1, compute the asymptotic speed or growth exponent explicitly.

title: Prime Langford pairings
plain: Arrange two copies each of 1 to n so the two copies of k sit exactly the k-th prime apart. For which n is this possible?
math: Determine all $n$ for which $1,1,\dots,n,n$ can be arranged so the two copies of $k$ are $p_k$ positions apart.

title: Prime Golomb rulers
plain: Find the shortest ruler with marks only at prime positions where all distances between marks are different.
math: For each $n$, determine the minimal $L$ such that some set of $n$ primes in an interval of length $L$ has all pairwise differences distinct; find its asymptotics.

title: Three large consecutive factors
plain: Show infinitely many n have n, n + 1 and n + 2 each with a prime factor bigger than n^0.9.
math: Prove infinitely many $n$ with $\min\{P(n),P(n+1),P(n+2)\}>n^{0.9}$.

title: Sidon sets of seven-free numbers
plain: Find the largest subset of the seven-free numbers up to N with all pairwise sums distinct, up to a constant factor.
math: Determine the order of magnitude of $\max\{|A|:A\subseteq\{n\le N:7\notin n\},\ A\text{ Sidon}\}$.

title: Roth for seven-free numbers
plain: Show every subset of the seven-free numbers that keeps a fixed fraction of them contains three in arithmetic progression.
math: Prove for every $\delta>0$ and large $N$, every $A\subseteq\{n\le N:7\notin n\}$ with $|A|\ge\delta\#\{n\le N:7\notin n\}$ contains a nontrivial 3-term AP.

title: Hexagonal Lebesgue covering
plain: Find the smallest convex shape that can cover every set of diameter 1, if covering is by translation only, not rotation.
math: Determine $\min\{\mathrm{area}(K):K$ convex, every set of diameter $1$ has a translate inside $K\}$, and prove the minimiser is unique.

title: Random sequential prime-sum packing
plain: Add random numbers from 1 to N one at a time, keeping a number only if it forms no prime sum with any kept number. Find the final density.
math: Determine $\lim_N\mathbb{E}|A_N|/N$ for the random sequential independent set of the prime-sum graph on $[N]$.

title: Prime factor plus digit sum
plain: Add the largest prime factor of n to its digit sum. Every tested start ends in 6 → 9 → 12. Prove all do, which needs ruling out endless chains of primes p → p + digit sum.
math: For $f(n)=P(n)+s_{10}(n)$, prove every orbit with $n\ge2$ reaches the cycle $(6,9,12)$.

title: Square subtraction with prime piles
plain: In the game where you subtract a square, show infinitely many prime pile sizes are losing positions.
math: Prove infinitely many primes are P-positions of the subtract-a-square game.

title: Treewidth of the prime-sum graph
plain: Find the treewidth of the prime-sum graph on 1 to 2n asymptotically.
math: Prove $\mathrm{tw}(\Pi_{2n})\sim c\,n$ for the prime-sum graph and determine $c$.

title: Clique minors in the prime-sum graph
plain: Show the prime-sum graph on 1 to 2n has a complete minor of size about n over the square root of log n.
math: Prove $h(\Pi_{2n})=\Theta(n/\sqrt{\log n})$.

title: Optimal square-sum circle gaps
plain: Among all arrangements of 1 to N in a circle where neighbours sum to squares, minimise the largest difference between neighbours. Find the order of the minimum.
math: Determine the order of $\min_{C}\max_{i}|v_{i+1}-v_i|$ over Hamiltonian cycles $C$ of $S_N$.

title: Hadwiger's true constant
plain: If graphs needing many colors need not contain a full complete-graph minor, find how large a complete minor they must contain.
math: Find $c^*=\liminf_{t}\min\{h(G)/t:\chi(G)\ge t\}$, where $h$ is the Hadwiger number.

title: Icosahedral monotile
plain: Find a single 3D tile that fills space and forces five-fold, icosahedral symmetry in every tiling.
math: Find $T\subset\mathbb{R}^3$ tiling space such that every tiling by $T$ has icosahedral symmetry in its hull, or prove none exists.

title: Minimal four-color proof
plain: The four color theorem's proof checks a big list of map configurations. Find the smallest list that works.
math: Determine the minimum size of an unavoidable set of reducible configurations for planar triangulations, with proof of minimality.

title: Perfect Minesweeper
plain: What is the exact chance that perfect play wins expert Minesweeper?
math: Compute $\sup_\sigma\Pr(\text{win})$ for $30\times16$ with 99 uniform mines and a safe first click.

title: Readable Riemann
plain: The 2026 Riemann proof is a giant machine-checked archive. Write a proof people can read.
math: Give a proof of the Riemann hypothesis of at most 100 pages acceptable to expert referees.

title: Short Riemann
plain: Shrink the 2026 machine-checked Riemann proof drastically.
math: Give a Lean 4 proof of `RiemannHypothesis` in at most 10,000 lines beyond Mathlib.

title: Small Hadwiger counterexample
plain: The claimed counterexamples to Hadwiger's conjecture are astronomically large. Find one under a million vertices.
math: Find $G$ with $|V(G)|<10^6$ and $h(G)<\chi(G)$, or prove every counterexample is larger.

title: Explicit Navier–Stokes blow-up
plain: Write down a forced Navier–Stokes blow-up as an explicit formula instead of a computer-assisted construction.
math: Give closed-form smooth $u_0,f$ on $\mathbb{R}^3$ for which the Navier–Stokes solution blows up in finite time.

title: Two of four
plain: Show infinitely many primes p have at least one more prime among p + 2, 2p + 1, 2p + 3.
math: Prove infinitely many primes $p$ have at least one of $p+2,\,2p+1,\,2p+3$ prime.

title: Unbounded Prime Nim
plain: Do the Prime Nim values grow without limit?
math: Decide whether $\sup_n G(n)=\infty$ for the prime subtraction game.

title: Rounded corners
plain: The inside corner of the hallway is rounded. Find the best sofa for every rounding radius.
math: For each $\rho\ge0$, determine the optimal sofa for the width-1 corridor whose inner corner is a quarter-circle of radius $\rho$.

title: Kakeya discs
plain: What is the least volume needed to turn a flat disc to every orientation?
math: Determine $\inf$ volume of sets in $\mathbb{R}^3$ containing a unit disc in every orientation (positive by Marstrand), with an extremizer.

title: 3-SAT at density 4
plain: Give a fast algorithm that solves almost all random 3-SAT puzzles up to clause density 4.
math: Give a polynomial-time algorithm finding satisfying assignments of random 3-SAT with density $4.0$ with probability $1-o(1)$.

title: Prime ladders
plain: Change one digit at a time, staying prime. Show any two k-digit primes are linked by at most k + 1 steps.
math: In the graph on $k$-digit primes joined when differing in one decimal digit, prove $\operatorname{diam}\le k+1$ for all $k$.

title: Largest-factor Collatz stopping time
plain: How many steps does the largest-factor Collatz map take, on average, to reach 1?
math: Prove $\frac1x\sum_{n\le x}T(n)\sim c\log x$ for the stopping time $T$ of $f$, and compute $c$.

title: Ringel for forests
plain: Split a complete graph on 2m + 1 vertices into identical copies of any given forest with m edges.
math: Prove $K_{2m+1}$ decomposes into $2m+1$ copies of any forest with $m$ edges.

title: Zigzag sofa
plain: A hallway turns right, then left after distance d. Find the best sofa for every d.
math: For each $d>0$, determine the optimal sofa for the width-1 corridor with two opposite right turns separated by $d$.

title: Spiral staircase
plain: What is the biggest convex box-like object that can be carried up a given spiral staircase?
math: Maximize volume over convex bodies admissible in a helical tube of square cross-section $1$, radius $2$, pitch $3$.

title: Geodesic squares on surfaces
plain: Every smooth closed curve on a convex surface should pass through the corners of a square made of shortest paths.
math: Prove every smooth simple closed curve on a smooth convex surface inscribes a geodesic quadrilateral with equal sides and equal diagonals.

title: Hat opaque set
plain: Find the shortest set of walls that blocks every straight line through the hat tile.
math: Determine the minimal total length of an opaque set for the hat polygon.

title: Hat spectrum is a Cantor set
plain: Show the energy levels of a particle hopping on a hat tiling form a dust of measure zero.
math: Prove the spectrum of the adjacency operator on the hat graph is a Cantor set of Lebesgue measure zero.

title: Smallest force for blow-up
plain: How weak can the push be and still make viscous fluid blow up?
math: Find the optimal exponent $a$ with $\inf\{\|f\|_{L^\infty}: \text{NS from rest blows up}\}\asymp \nu^{a}$.

title: Forced SQG blow-up
plain: Copy the 2026 forced Navier–Stokes blow-up for the surface quasi-geostrophic equation.
math: Construct smooth compactly supported $f$ such that forced SQG on $\mathbb{R}^2$ from rest blows up in finite time.

title: Prime Nim is not simple
plain: Show Prime Nim losing positions cannot be detected by shallow constant-depth circuits.
math: Prove the indicator of P-positions of the prime subtraction game (in binary) is not in $\mathsf{AC}^0$.

title: Lean golf is hard to approximate
plain: Not only is the shortest basic-tactic proof hard to find; even a roughly short one is.
math: Prove intro/apply/exact/rfl proof minimization admits no constant-factor approximation unless P = NP.

title: Navier–Stokes blow-up in Isabelle
plain: Re-check the 2026 Navier–Stokes blow-up in a completely different proof assistant.
math: Formalize in Isabelle/HOL the existence of a smooth forced finite-time blow-up of 3D Navier–Stokes.

title: Prime Nim is not automatic
plain: No finite machine reading digits can recognize Prime Nim losing positions.
math: Prove the P-position set is not $k$-automatic for any base $k\ge2$.

title: Integer-bijective Keller map
plain: Find a polynomial map with Jacobian 1 that shuffles integer points perfectly but has no polynomial inverse.
math: Find $F\in\mathbb{Z}[x]^n$, $\det DF\equiv1$, inducing a bijection of $\mathbb{Z}^n$ but not a polynomial automorphism.

title: Firebreak with wind
plain: How long must a firebreak be to save a round town from a wind-driven fire?
math: For front speed $a+b\cos\theta$ and a disc town at distance $D$, find the minimal length of a curve built at speed $\sigma$ that protects the town.

title: 5n+1 largest-factor cycles
plain: Use 5n + 1 instead of 3n + 1 in the largest-factor map. Show it has only finitely many loops.
math: For $f_5(n)=n/2$ (even), $P(5n+1)$ (odd), prove $f_5$ has finitely many cycles.

title: Twin-free stretches
plain: Find long stretches full of primes but containing no twin primes.
math: Prove there are intervals $[x,x+(\log x)^{1.1}]$ with $\ge(\log x)^{0.05}$ primes but no twin pair, for infinitely many $x$.

title: Big factors of p² + p + 1
plain: For primes p, show p² + p + 1 often has a very large prime factor.
math: Prove $P(p^2+p+1)>p^{1.5}$ for infinitely many primes $p$.

title: Isoperimetric sofa
plain: Among sofas with a fixed perimeter, find the one with largest area that turns the corner.
math: For each $L$, maximize area over corridor-admissible sets of perimeter $\le L$.

title: Kayles on square sums
plain: Players take turns claiming numbers, never next to a claimed one in the square-sum graph. Who wins?
math: Determine the node-Kayles outcome on $S_N$ for all $N$.

title: Cops on square sums
plain: How many cops catch a robber moving along square-sum links?
math: Determine $c(S_N)$, the cop number of the square-sum graph, for all large $N$.

title: Random hat parking
plain: Drop hat tiles at random without overlap until no more fit. What fraction gets covered?
math: Compute the jamming density of random sequential adsorption of hats (random rotations from the kite grid) in the plane.

title: Random walks on square sums
plain: How long does a random walk on the square-sum graph take to forget its starting point?
math: Determine the mixing time of simple random walk on the giant component of $S_N$ up to constants.

title: Sudoku completions are log-normal
plain: Erase half a random Sudoku. The number of ways to refill it should follow a log-normal law.
math: For a random $9\times9$ grid with a uniformly random half of cells erased, prove $\log(\#\text{completions})$ is asymptotically normal under the natural $n^2\times n^2$ scaling.

title: Cube-sum colors
plain: Join numbers that add up to a perfect cube. Show a fixed number of colors always suffices.
math: For $C_N$ with $a\sim b\iff a+b$ a cube, prove $\sup_N\chi(C_N)<\infty$ and find it.

title: Hat dominating sets
plain: Find the smallest fraction of hat tiles that touch every other tile.
math: Compute the asymptotic domination density of the hat adjacency graph.

title: Spectre vs hat dimers
plain: Show the spectre tiling and the hat tiling have different domino-covering entropies.
math: Prove the dimer entropies per vertex of the spectre and hat adjacency graphs differ.

title: Doubled-twin constant
plain: Assuming deep but standard conjectures, find the exact count of doubled twins up to x.
math: Assuming the Elliott–Halberstam conjecture, prove a lower bound $\gg x/(\log x)^4$ for doubled twins with $p$ and one other form prime.

title: Emirp sieve
plain: Show infinitely many primes have reversals with no small prime factors.
math: Prove infinitely many primes $p$ have $\operatorname{rev}(p)$ with all prime factors $>p^{0.1}$.

title: Lonely runner, bounded speeds
plain: Prove the lonely runner conjecture whenever all speeds are at most 10 times the number of runners.
math: Prove $\sup_t\min_i\|tv_i\|\ge\frac1{n+1}$ for all distinct $v_i\le10n$.

title: Lonely runners in 3D
plain: Runners move in three dimensions on a cube that wraps around. Find the guaranteed loneliness.
math: For $n$ pairwise independent $v_i\in\mathbb{Z}^3$, find the optimal $\delta_n$ with $\sup_t\min_i\|tv_i\|_{\mathbb{T}^3,\infty}\ge\delta_n$.

title: Delayed fire on hexagons
plain: On a honeycomb grid, firefighters arrive one turn late. Find how many per turn are needed.
math: On the hexagonal lattice with 3-neighbour spread and one-turn protection delay, find the least per-turn budget containing a single fire.

title: Wind-driven fire in 3D
plain: In 3D, fire spreads in five of six directions because of wind. How many firefighters per turn are needed?
math: On $\mathbb{Z}^3$ with spread to all neighbours except $-e_1$, find the least per-turn budget containing a single fire.

title: Keller maps of degree 4
plain: Show that every 3D polynomial map of degree at most 4 with constant Jacobian has a polynomial inverse.
math: Prove $F:\mathbb{C}^3\to\mathbb{C}^3$, $\deg F\le4$, $\det DF\in\mathbb{C}^\times$ implies $F$ is an automorphism.

title: Hyperbolic lonely runners
plain: Runners move along closed paths on a hyperbolic surface. Show one eventually gets far from all others.
math: For geodesic flows on a closed hyperbolic surface along $n$ distinct primitive closed geodesics, prove a uniform separation time exists, with optimal bound.

title: Hex on hat boards, large
plain: Solve Hex on hat-tiled boards of side 9.
math: Determine the winner of Hex on the hat-tiled rhombus board of side 9, with an explicit strategy.

title: Pipe-bend sofa, exact
plain: Find and prove the optimal solid for a round pipe with a right-angle bend.
math: Determine the maximal volume and an optimizer for the diameter-1 circular pipe with a right-angle bend.

title: Random-turn Prime Nim
plain: In Prime Nim where a coin flip decides who moves, find the exact winning chance from a pile of n.
math: For random-turn play of the prime subtraction game, compute $\lim_n$ of the value from pile $n$, if it exists.

title: Fire spotting threshold
plain: Embers jump ahead of a fire. Find the jump probability where firefighting becomes hopeless.
math: On $\mathbb{Z}^2$, a burning cell also ignites a uniformly random cell at distance $\le r$ with probability $q$. Find $q^*(r,k)$ beyond which $k$ protections per turn fail a.s.

title: Smoke-free corridor
plain: Show a corridor's smoke clears in a predictable time when air flows through it.
math: For advection–diffusion in a periodic corridor with Stokes flow, find the sharp exponential decay rate of a passive scalar in terms of geometry.

title: Sofa with a pillar
plain: A thin pillar stands in the corner of the hallway. Find the best sofa that gets around it.
math: Determine the optimal sofa for the width-1 corridor with a point obstacle at $(1/2,1/2)$ from the outer corner.

title: Exotic shuffles
plain: For which deck sizes do the three-pile shuffles generate every possible arrangement?
math: Determine all $n$ for which the six 3-pile shuffles generate $S_{3n}$ or $A_{3n}$.

title: Sofa stability
plain: Show that any sofa nearly as big as Gerver's must look nearly like Gerver's.
math: Prove a quantitative stability bound: $A(S)\ge A_G-\varepsilon$ implies $d_H(S,G)\le C\varepsilon^{\alpha}$ up to rigid motion.

title: Kissing spectres
plain: How many spectre tiles can touch one spectre without overlapping?
math: Determine the maximal number of interior-disjoint congruent spectres meeting a fixed one.

title: Spectre percolation
plain: Show percolation on the spectre tiling and the hat tiling have different thresholds.
math: Prove $p_c^{\text{site}}(\text{spectre})\ne p_c^{\text{site}}(\text{hat})$.

title: Hat Ising bounds
plain: Pin down the critical temperature of magnets on a hat tiling to within one percent.
math: Prove two-sided bounds on $T_c$ for the hat-graph Ising model with ratio $\le1.01$.

title: Seven-free almost-Sophie-Germain
plain: Show infinitely many primes p avoid the digit 7 and have 2p + 1 with few prime factors.
math: Prove infinitely many 7-free primes $p$ have $\Omega(2p+1)\le3$.

title: Sudoku symmetry breaking
plain: Show that most big Sudoku grids have no symmetry at all.
math: Prove the proportion of $n^2\times n^2$ Sudoku grids with nontrivial automorphism tends to 0.

title: Twin hats
plain: Find a pair of different tiles that can each tile the plane only together, aperiodically, with a matching rule nobody has found yet.
math: Find two polykites $A,B$ with $\le 6$ kites each, neither tiling alone, that together tile $\mathbb{R}^2$ only aperiodically.

title: Self-similar fire
plain: Show a fire spreading with random fuel forms a shape that grows at a fixed limiting speed in every direction.
math: For first-passage percolation on the hat graph with i.i.d. exponential weights, prove the limit shape exists and is not a polygon.

title: Lorenz attractor dimension
plain: Pin down the fractal dimension of the classic Lorenz attractor to two decimals, rigorously.
math: For $\sigma=10,\beta=8/3,\rho=28$, prove $2.06\le\dim_H\mathcal{A}\le2.07$.

title: Wythoff Prime Nim
plain: With two piles, remove a prime from one pile or the same prime from both. Describe the losing positions.
math: Characterize the P-positions of the two-pile game with moves $(a,b)\to(a-p,b),(a,b-p),(a-p,b-p)$, $p$ prime.

title: Smallest-factor Collatz stopping time
plain: How many steps does the smallest-odd-factor Collatz map take to reach 1, on average?
math: Determine the asymptotic order of $\frac1x\sum_{n\le x}T_g(n)$ for the stopping time of $g$.

title: Cube-sum connectivity
plain: Join numbers that add to a perfect cube. Show everything links up once N is large.
math: Prove $C_N$ ($a\sim b\iff a+b$ is a cube) is connected for all sufficiently large $N$.

title: Keller maps over finite fields
plain: Count the polynomial maps of three variables over a finite field with constant Jacobian that happen to be bijections.
math: For $F\in\mathbb{F}_p[x,y,z]^3$ of degree $\le3$ with $\det DF\in\mathbb{F}_p^\times$, find the asymptotic proportion inducing bijections of $\mathbb{F}_p^3$ as $p\to\infty$.

title: Unit-distance barrier
plain: Show the 2026 number-field method for many equal distances can never reach exponent 1.1.
math: Prove every construction of the Alon–Bloom–Gowers–…–Sawin type (lattices from number fields of bounded class-field degree) gives $u(n)\le n^{1.1}$.

title: Polykite growth constant
plain: Count shapes made of n kites. Find the exponential growth rate to three digits.
math: Let $k_n$ count polykites with $n$ kites up to congruence. Prove $k_n^{1/n}\to\lambda$ and compute $\lambda$ to 3 digits.

title: Hat treewidth
plain: Find exactly how hard hat-tiled regions are to break into small pieces.
math: Prove the treewidth of $n$-tile hat patches is $\sim c\sqrt n$ and compute $c$.

title: Hat contact process
plain: An infection spreads between neighbouring hat tiles and heals at random. Bound the critical infection rate tightly.
math: For the contact process on the hat graph, prove $\lambda_c$ lies in an explicit interval of relative width $\le 2\%$.

title: Four-arc sofa
plain: Find the best sofa whose outline uses at most four circular arcs and straight pieces.
math: Maximize area over admissible sofas whose boundary consists of at most four circular arcs plus segments.

title: Hat drum's first mode
plain: Strike a hat-shaped drum. Show its lowest tone vibrates with a single peak.
math: Prove the first Dirichlet eigenfunction of the hat polygon has exactly one interior critical point.

title: Seven-free primes in short intervals
plain: Show seven-free primes appear in every reasonably short interval.
math: Prove $[x,x+x^{0.6}]$ contains a prime with no digit 7 for all large $x$.

title: Three-pile shuffle cutoff
plain: Random three-pile shuffles mix a deck suddenly, after a precise number of shuffles. Find it.
math: For random compositions of uniformly chosen 3-pile shuffles on $3n$ cards, prove total-variation cutoff at $c\log n$ and find $c$.

title: Hat corona limit
plain: Surround a hat by layers of hats again and again. The growing blob approaches a fixed shape. Find it.
math: Prove the scaled $k$-th coronas of a hat converge in Hausdorff distance and identify the limit shape.

title: The 4p+1 funnel, almost always
plain: Show almost every prime falls into the eight-prime loop of the 4p + 1 map.
math: Prove the set of primes whose $p\mapsto P(4p+1)$ orbit enters the 8-cycle has relative density 1 among primes.

title: Largest factor of consecutive-prime products
plain: Show that p_n·p_(n+1) + 1 has a prime factor much bigger than p_(n+1), infinitely often.
math: Prove $P(p_np_{n+1}+1)>p_{n+1}^{1.5}$ for infinitely many $n$.

title: Smooth shifted primes in two bases
plain: Find infinitely many primes p for which p − 1 has only small prime factors and p has no digit 7.
math: Prove infinitely many 7-free primes $p$ with $P(p-1)\le p^{0.3}$.

title: Square-sum connectivity
plain: Show the square-sum graph cannot be split by removing fewer vertices than its smallest degree.
math: Prove $\kappa(S_N)=\delta(S_N)$ for all large $N$.

title: Odd-cycle-free square sums
plain: How many numbers up to N can you keep so the square-sum graph on them has no odd cycle?
math: Determine $\max\{|A|:A\subseteq[N],\ S_N[A]\text{ bipartite}\}/N$ asymptotically.

title: Midpoint map as a random walk
plain: Show that, for a random large start, the logarithm of the midpoint-prime orbit moves like a Gaussian random walk.
math: Prove that for $n$ uniform in $[x,2x]$, the distribution of $\log m^{k}(n)-\log n$ for $k=\lfloor\log x\rfloor$ converges after normalization to a Gaussian.

title: Internal DLA on hats
plain: Release walkers one at a time from a hat tile; each stops at the first unoccupied tile. Show the occupied cluster becomes a round disc.
math: For internal DLA on the hat adjacency graph with $n$ particles, prove the cluster rescaled by $\sqrt n$ converges to a Euclidean disc (with tile centres as positions).

title: Rotor walks on the spectre
plain: A rotor walk on the spectre tiling should stay within bounded distance of a random walk's expected behaviour. Prove the discrepancy is bounded.
math: For rotor-router aggregation on the spectre graph with $n$ particles, prove the cluster differs from a disc of area $n$ by $O(\log n)$ in Hausdorff distance.

title: Hot spots on the hat
plain: Heat a hat-shaped insulated plate. Decide whether the hottest point eventually sits on the boundary.
math: Decide whether a second Neumann eigenfunction of the hat polygon attains its maximum only on $\partial\Omega$.

title: Square-sum labelling of caterpillars
plain: Label the vertices of a tree with 1 to n so that every edge sums to a perfect square. Show every caterpillar of maximum degree 3 can be done, once it is large.
math: Prove every caterpillar with $n\ge n_0$ vertices and maximum degree $\le3$ admits a bijection $V\to[n]$ with $\ell(u)+\ell(v)$ a square for every edge $uv$.

title: The square-sum avoidance game
plain: Players take turns choosing unused numbers from 1 to N. Whoever picks a number summing to a square with any already-chosen number loses. Decide the winner for all large N.
math: Determine the outcome class of the avoidance game on $S_N$ (normal play, a move creating an $S_N$-edge inside the chosen set loses) for all sufficiently large $N$.

title: Greedy independent sets in square sums
plain: Pick random numbers up to N one by one, skipping any that sum to a square with something already picked. How many do you end with?
math: Determine the asymptotic size of the random greedy independent set in $S_N$, in probability.

title: Hamiltonian cycles in hat patches
plain: Count closed tours visiting every tile of a large hat-tiled region once. Find the exponential growth rate per tile.
math: For hat-tiled $L$-balls with $n$ tiles, prove $(\#\text{Hamiltonian cycles})^{1/n}\to\beta$ and determine $\beta$ to 3 digits rigorously.

title: Prime Nim game graph
plain: Prime Nim has losing positions with a hidden mod-structure. Show the losing positions are equidistributed in residue classes mod 3.
math: Prove $\#\{n\le x:G(n)=0,\ n\equiv a\ (3)\}\sim\frac13\#\{n\le x:G(n)=0\}$ for each $a$.

title: Affine prime maps, quantitative
plain: Show that for the map p ↦ largest prime factor of 3p + 4, almost every prime reaches its loop within about log log p steps.
math: For $p\mapsto P(3p+4)$, prove that for all but $o(\pi(x))$ primes $p\le x$ the orbit of $p$ enters its (unique observed) 7-cycle within $C\log\log p$ steps.

title: The angel on the hat
plain: An angel moves up to k tiles per turn on a hat tiling; a devil deletes one tile per turn. Find the least k for which the angel escapes forever.
math: Determine the least $k$ such that the angel of power $k$ (moves to any tile within graph distance $k$) wins against the devil on every hat tiling's adjacency graph.

title: Square-sum paths with chosen ends
plain: Show you can line up 1 to N with neighbours summing to squares, starting and ending at almost any two numbers you choose.
math: Prove $S_N$ contains a Hamiltonian path whose endpoints can be prescribed arbitrarily among vertices of degree $\ge3$, for all large $N$.

title: Square-sum Ramsey of paths
plain: Two-colour the numbers 1 to N. Show some colour contains a chain of length L where neighbours sum to squares, with L growing like a power of N.
math: Prove every 2-colouring of $[N]$ has a monochromatic path in $S_N$ of length $\ge N^{c}$ for some $c>0$, and find the optimal $c$.

title: Isoperimetric profile of the spectre
plain: Among all clusters of n spectre tiles, find the smallest possible perimeter, asymptotically, with the exact constant.
math: Prove $\min\{|\partial S|:S$ a union of $n$ tiles in a spectre tiling$\}\sim c\sqrt n$ and determine $c$.

title: Gerver sofa contact points
plain: Prove Gerver's sofa touches the corridor walls in exactly the pattern Gerver described at every moment of its optimal motion, and that the motion is unique.
math: Prove the optimal motion of Gerver's sofa through the unit corridor is unique up to time reparametrization.

title: Spectre quantum walk spreading
plain: A quantum particle hopping on the spectre tiling should spread at a rate strictly between localization and free motion. Compute the exponent.
math: For $H$ the adjacency operator of a spectre tiling and $\psi_0=\delta_o$, prove $\langle|X|^2\rangle_T\asymp T^{2\beta}$ and determine $\beta$.

title: Kissing numbers of polykite families
plain: Show the hat's family of shapes has a kissing number that jumps at exactly one parameter value.
math: For Tile$(a,b)$, $a,b>0$, let $k(a,b)$ be the kissing number (congruent copies, reflections allowed). Prove $k$ is piecewise constant with finitely many jumps and find them.

title: Graceful forests from caterpillar seeds
plain: Show forests made of large caterpillars plus one arbitrary tree are graceful-forest labelable.
math: Prove every forest $T\cup C_1\cup\dots\cup C_k$ with $T$ any tree and $C_i$ caterpillars each of size $\ge|T|$ admits a bijection $V\to\{0,\dots,m+k\}$ with distinct edge differences.

title: Hats in a torus
plain: Hats tile the plane only non-periodically, so they cannot tile a flat torus. Find the smallest uncovered fraction for packing hats on a flat torus of area A.
math: Let $g(A)$ be the least uncovered area over packings of congruent hats in flat tori of area $A$. Prove $g(A)\to\infty$ and determine its growth order in $A$.

title: Spectre chromatic number of distances
plain: Colour points of the plane so no two points at a distance equal to a spectre edge length or diagonal share a colour. Find the colours needed.
math: Let $D$ be the set of distances between vertices of the spectre polygon. Determine $\chi(\mathbb{R}^2;D)$.

title: Chromatic number of prime-difference plus square-sum
plain: Join two numbers if their sum is a square or their difference is prime. Find the colours needed for all positive integers.
math: Determine $\chi(G)$ for $G$ on $\mathbb{N}$ with $a\sim b$ iff $a+b$ is a square or $|a-b|$ is prime.

title: The hat is not spectral
plain: Fuglede's conjecture predicts that a shape that cannot tile by translations has no orthogonal basis of exponentials. Prove this for the hat.
math: Prove there is no $\Lambda\subset\mathbb{R}^2$ with $\{e^{2\pi i\lambda\cdot x}\}_{\lambda\in\Lambda}$ an orthogonal basis of $L^2(\text{hat})$.

title: Lost in a hat-shaped forest
plain: You are lost in a forest shaped like a hat, position and orientation unknown. Find the shortest path guaranteed to get you out.
math: Determine Bellman's escape length for the hat polygon: the least length of a curve such that every congruent placement of it inside the hat meets the boundary.

title: Waring with seven-free cubes
plain: Find the fewest cubes of seven-free numbers needed to write every large number, and prove it.
math: Determine the least $s$ such that every sufficiently large integer is a sum of $s$ cubes of positive 7-free integers.

title: Counting square-sum chains
plain: Count the ways to line up 1 to N with neighbours summing to squares. Find the leading growth.
math: Let $h(N)$ be the number of Hamiltonian paths of $S_N$. Prove $\log h(N)=(\tfrac12+o(1))N\log N$.

title: Seven-free Beatty primes
plain: Show infinitely many primes of the form ⌊n√2⌋ contain no digit 7.
math: Prove infinitely many primes $p=\lfloor n\sqrt2\rfloor$ with no decimal digit 7.

title: Seven-free primes as an additive basis
plain: Show every large number is a sum of a bounded number of seven-free primes.
math: Prove there is $k$ such that every sufficiently large integer of suitable parity is a sum of at most $k$ primes with no decimal digit 7, and give an explicit $k$.

title: Discrete sofa
plain: Slide and rotate a polyomino by unit steps and quarter turns around the corner of a corridor k cells wide. Find the largest area possible, asymptotically.
math: Let $D(k)$ be the maximal number of cells of a polyomino that can pass the width-$k$ L-shaped corridor of $\mathbb{Z}^2$ by unit translations and $90^\circ$ rotations about lattice points (staying inside at all times). Prove $D(k)\sim ck^2$ and find $c$.

title: Spectre electrical resistance
plain: Find the exact asymptotic electrical resistance between two far-apart spectre tiles, with unit resistors on edges.
math: Prove $R(o,x)=\kappa\log|x|+O(1)$ on spectre tilings and compute $\kappa$ in closed form.

title: Hard-core on the hat
plain: Place particles on hat tiles with no two neighbours both occupied. Show the gas freezes into an ordered state at high density.
math: For the hard-core model on the hat graph, prove a phase transition: non-uniqueness of Gibbs measures for all activities $\lambda\ge\lambda_0$.

title: Seven-free Chen primes in progressions
plain: Show infinitely many seven-free primes p in every allowable residue class have p + 2 with at most three prime factors.
math: For each $q$ and admissible $a$, prove infinitely many 7-free primes $p\equiv a\ (q)$ with $\Omega(p+2)\le3$.

title: Largest factor of the midpoint
plain: For consecutive primes p < q, look at the largest prime factor of (p + q)/2. Show it exceeds p^0.5 for a positive fraction.
math: Prove $\#\{n\le x: P(\tfrac{p_n+p_{n+1}}2)>p_n^{1/2}\}\gg \pi(x)$.

title: Prime-sum Hamiltonian cycles through every edge
plain: Show every edge of the prime-sum graph on 1 to 2n lies on a full prime circle.
math: Prove for all large $n$ every edge of the prime-sum graph on $[2n]$ lies on a Hamiltonian cycle.

title: Polykite growth: one more digit
plain: Pin the exponential growth rate of n-kite shapes to within one percent, rigorously.
math: Prove explicit bounds $a\le\lambda\le b$ with $b/a\le1.01$ for the polykite growth constant $\lambda=\lim k_n^{1/n}$.

title: Midpoint-prime orbit lengths
plain: Find the average number of steps the midpoint-prime map takes to reach 1, on a logarithmic scale.
math: For the midpoint-prime map $m$, prove $\frac1x\sum_{n\le x}\frac{T_m(n)}{\log n}\to c$ and compute $c$, where $T_m(n)=\min\{k:m^k(n)=1\}$.

title: Many loops for affine prime maps
plain: Show the number of separate loops of p ↦ largest prime factor of ap + 1 grows without bound as a grows.
math: Let $N(a)$ be the number of periodic orbits of $p\mapsto P(ap+1)$ on primes. Prove $\limsup_{a\to\infty}N(a)=\infty$.

title: Snort on square sums
plain: Two players colour numbers up to N, one red and one blue. Neither may colour a number summing to a square with one of the opponent's colour. The player who cannot move loses. Decide who wins for large N.
math: Determine the outcome of the partizan game Snort on $S_N$ for all sufficiently large $N$.

title: Maker–Breaker square-sum triangles
plain: Maker and Breaker alternately claim numbers. Maker wins by owning three numbers whose pairwise sums are all squares. Decide who wins on 1 to N for large N.
math: Determine the winner of the Maker–Breaker game on $[N]$ whose winning sets are the triangles of $S_N$, for all sufficiently large $N$.

title: Entering the 4p+1 loop
plain: Show a typical prime enters the 4p + 1 map's eight-prime loop in about log log p steps.
math: For $p\mapsto P(4p+1)$, prove that the number of steps to enter the 8-cycle is $\sim c\log\log p$ for all but $o(\pi(x))$ primes $p\le x$, and find $c$.

title: Square-plus-one collisions
plain: Count pairs n ≠ m up to x for which n² + 1 and m² + 1 have the same largest prime factor.
math: Find the asymptotic number of pairs $n<m\le x$ with $P(n^2+1)=P(m^2+1)$.

title: Seven-free square-sum chains
plain: Take only the numbers up to N with no digit 7. Show they can be lined up so neighbours always sum to perfect squares, for large N.
math: Let $A_N=\{n\le N: 7\notin n\}$. Prove $S_N[A_N]$ has a Hamiltonian path for all sufficiently large $N$.

title: Long loops for affine prime maps
plain: As a and b vary, the loops of p ↦ largest prime factor of ap + b get longer and longer. Prove loop lengths are unbounded.
math: Prove $\sup_{a,b}\max\{\text{length of a cycle of } p\mapsto P(ap+b)\}=\infty$.

title: Max-cut of the square-sum graph
plain: Split the numbers up to N into two groups to cut as many square-sum pairs as possible. Find how far above one half you can get.
math: Prove $\mathrm{MaxCut}(S_N)=\big(\tfrac12+(c+o(1))N^{-1/4}\big)e(S_N)$ and determine $c$.

title: Seven-free primes with prime digit sum
plain: Show infinitely many primes have no digit 7 and a digit sum that is itself prime.
math: Prove infinitely many primes $p$ free of the decimal digit 7 with $s_{10}(p)$ prime.

title: The 89–233 basin
plain: The square-plus-one map has the loop 89 ↔ 233. Each prime has only finitely many direct predecessors, so the question is whether the tree of predecessors is infinite. Decide whether infinitely many starting numbers fall into the loop.
math: Decide whether infinitely many $n$ have $Q^k(n)\in\{89,233\}$ for some $k$, where $Q(n)=P(n^2+1)$.

title: Simple spectrum of the hat
plain: Show no two vibration frequencies of the hat-shaped drum coincide.
math: Prove every Dirichlet eigenvalue of the hat polygon is simple.

title: Node Kayles on square sums
plain: Players alternately pick an unused number up to N that does not sum to a square with any picked number. Last to move wins. Decide the winner for large N.
math: Determine the outcome of Node Kayles on $S_N$ for all sufficiently large $N$.

title: Square-sum ordering with bounded displacement
plain: Order all positive integers so neighbours always sum to squares, and no number moves more than a fixed distance from its natural place.
math: Decide whether there is a bijection $\pi:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ with $\pi(i)+\pi(i+1)$ always a square and $\sup_i|\pi(i)-i|/\sqrt i<\infty$.

title: The 7p+4 funnel, almost always
plain: Show almost every prime eventually falls into the 12-cycle of the 7p + 4 map.
math: Prove the primes whose $p\mapsto P(7p+4)$ orbit enters its 12-cycle have relative density 1.

title: Prime Nim on Gaussian integers
plain: Play Prime Nim with Gaussian integers: subtract a Gaussian prime staying in the first quadrant. Show losing positions have density zero.
math: For positions $a+bi$ with $a,b\ge0$ and moves $z\mapsto z-\pi$ with $\pi$ a Gaussian prime and the result in the closed first quadrant, prove the P-positions have density 0.

title: Codes avoiding square distances
plain: Find the largest set of binary strings of length n in which no two differ in a perfect-square number of positions. Find the exponential rate.
math: Let $A(n)$ be the largest $C\subseteq\{0,1\}^n$ with $d_H(x,y)$ never a positive perfect square for $x\ne y\in C$. Determine $\lim_n\frac1n\log_2A(n)$.

title: Turning a hat by 60 degrees
plain: Rotate a hat tile continuously by 60° inside a region of least possible area. Find that area.
math: Determine $\inf\{|E|: E\subset\mathbb{R}^2$ contains the trace of a continuous rigid motion carrying the unit hat to its rotation by $60^\circ$ about a point$\}$, and whether it is attained.

title: Square-sum triangle-free density
plain: Find the largest fraction of 1 to N you can keep with no three numbers whose pairwise sums are all perfect squares.
math: Determine $\lim_{N}\frac1N\max\{|A|:A\subseteq[N],\ A\text{ contains no triangle of }S_N\}$.

title: Seven-free primes with a large shifted factor
plain: Show a positive fraction of seven-free primes p have p − 1 with a prime factor bigger than p^0.6.
math: Prove $\#\{p\le x: p\ \text{7-free},\ P(p-1)>p^{0.6}\}\gg\pi_7(x)$.

title: Hot spots on Gerver's sofa
plain: Heat an insulated plate shaped like Gerver's sofa. Decide whether the hottest point eventually sits on the boundary.
math: Decide whether every second Neumann eigenfunction of Gerver's sofa attains its maximum and minimum only on the boundary.

title: The {5, 8} funnel
plain: Replace n by the sum of the largest prime factors of n and n + 1. Every start tested falls into the loop 5 → 8 → 5. Prove all do.
math: Let $f(n)=P(n)+P(n+1)$ (with $P(1)=1$). Prove every orbit of $f$ on $n\ge2$ enters the cycle $\{5,8\}$.

title: Two loops for P(n)+P(n+2)
plain: Replace n by P(n) + P(n + 2). Every tested start ends in 7 → 10 → 8 → 7 or in 9 → 14 → 9. Prove there are no other outcomes.
math: Prove every orbit of $n\mapsto P(n)+P(n+2)$ on $n\ge2$ enters $\{7,10,8\}$ or $\{9,14\}$.

title: Doubling the largest factor
plain: Replace n by twice its largest prime factor plus one. Every tested start falls into one loop of eight numbers. Prove all do.
math: Prove every orbit of $n\mapsto 2P(n)+1$ on $n\ge2$ enters the cycle $(7,15,11,23,47,95,39,27)$.

title: Doubling minus one
plain: Replace n by twice its largest prime factor minus one. Every tested start ends in 5 ↔ 9 or in the loop 37 → 73 → 145 → 57 → 37. Prove there is nothing else.
math: Prove every orbit of $n\mapsto 2P(n)-1$ on $n\ge2$ enters $\{5,9\}$ or $(37,73,145,57)$.

title: Three consecutive largest factors
plain: Replace n by P(n) + P(n + 1) + P(n + 2). Every tested start reaches the fixed point 14 or the loop 77 → 103 → 123 → 77. Prove it.
math: Prove every orbit of $n\mapsto P(n)+P(n+1)+P(n+2)$ on $n\ge2$ enters $\{14\}$ or $(77,103,123)$.

title: P(n)+P(n+1)−1
plain: Replace n by P(n) + P(n + 1) − 1. Every tested start ends in one of three loops. Prove these are the only ones.
math: Prove every orbit of $n\mapsto P(n)+P(n+1)-1$ on $n\ge2$ enters $(4,6,9,7,8)$, $(17,19,23,25)$ or $(167,173,201)$.

title: Three halves of the largest factor
plain: Replace n by the integer part of (3P(n) + 1)/2. Every tested start falls into the loop 3 → 5 → 8 → 3. Prove all do.
math: Prove every orbit of $n\mapsto\lfloor(3P(n)+1)/2\rfloor$ on $n\ge2$ enters $(3,5,8)$.

title: Three pairs
plain: Replace n by P(n) + P(2n + 1). Every tested start ends in one of three two-step loops: 13 ↔ 16, 30 ↔ 66, 36 ↔ 76. Prove it.
math: Prove every orbit of $n\mapsto P(n)+P(2n+1)$ on $n\ge2$ enters $\{13,16\}$, $\{30,66\}$ or $\{36,76\}$.

title: Last digits of consecutive largest factors
plain: Look at the last digits of P(n) and P(n + 1). Show the 16 possible pairs of last digits from {1, 3, 7, 9} occur equally often.
math: Prove $\#\{n\le x: P(n)\equiv a,\ P(n+1)\equiv b\ (10)\}\sim\frac{x}{16}$ for all $a,b\in\{1,3,7,9\}$.

title: Primes with equal binary and ternary digit sums
plain: Show infinitely many primes have the same digit sum in base 2 as in base 3.
math: Prove infinitely many primes $p$ with $s_2(p)=s_3(p)$.

title: A mixed Fermat equation
plain: Show the equation x² + y⁴ = z⁷ + 7 has only finitely many integer solutions.
math: Prove $x^2+y^4=z^7+7$ has finitely many solutions in integers.

title: Smooth p²+1
plain: Show infinitely many primes p have p² + 1 built only from primes below √p.
math: Prove infinitely many primes $p$ with $P(p^2+1)<p^{1/2}$.

title: Prime plus two seven-free squares
plain: Show every large number is a prime plus a sum of two squares whose bases have no digit 7.
math: Prove every sufficiently large $n$ is $p+a^2+b^2$ with $p$ prime and $a,b$ free of the decimal digit 7.

title: Linnik–Gallagher with seven-free primes
plain: Show every large even number is a seven-free prime plus a bounded number of powers of two.
math: Prove there is $K$ such that every sufficiently large even $n$ is $p+2^{a_1}+\dots+2^{a_k}$ with $k\le K$ and $p$ a 7-free prime.

title: Turán density of a twisted triple system
plain: Find the largest density of a 3-uniform hypergraph that avoids a specific six-vertex configuration of six triples.

title: Square-sum 4-cycle factors
plain: Split 1 to N into groups of four arranged in a cycle, so each pair of neighbours in a cycle sums to a square.
math: Prove $S_N$ has a $C_4$-factor for all sufficiently large $N\equiv0\pmod4$.

title: Prime Nim with Pythagorean primes
plain: In a variant of Prime Nim you may only remove 2 or a prime that is 1 mod 4. Show the losing positions have density zero.
math: For the subtraction game with move set $\{2\}\cup\{p\equiv1\ (4)\}$, prove the P-positions have natural density 0.

title: Partizan Prime Nim
plain: Left may remove a prime that is 1 mod 4, Right a prime that is 3 mod 4, from one pile. Describe the game values.
math: For the partizan subtraction game with $L=\{p\equiv1\ (4)\}$, $R=\{p\equiv3\ (4)\}$, prove every position is equal to a number or a number plus a switch of bounded temperature, and find the bound.

title: The Hamiltonicity game on square sums
plain: Maker and Breaker alternately claim edges of the square-sum graph. Maker wants a path through every number. Show Maker wins for large N.
math: Prove Maker wins the Maker–Breaker Hamiltonicity game on $S_N$ for all sufficiently large $N$.

title: Resolution lower bound for square-sum colouring
plain: Show any resolution proof that a large square-sum graph cannot be properly coloured with too few colours must be exponentially long.
math: Let $k(N)=\chi(S_N)-1$. Prove resolution refutations of the CNF "$S_N$ is $k(N)$-colourable" require size $2^{N^{\Omega(1)}}$.

title: Kneser graphs of square sums
plain: Take all k-element sets of numbers up to N that contain no square-sum pair, and join two if they are disjoint. Find the chromatic number.
math: Determine $\chi$ of the Kneser-type graph on independent $k$-sets of $S_N$ (adjacency = disjointness) for fixed $k$ and large $N$.

title: Prime-sum graph and perfect codes
plain: Decide for which n the prime-sum graph on 1 to 2n has a set of vertices that dominates every vertex exactly once.
math: Determine all $n$ for which the prime-sum graph on $[2n]$ has a perfect code (efficient dominating set).

title: Extremal square-sum subgraphs
plain: Find the largest number of edges in a subgraph of the square-sum graph with no 4-cycle.
math: Determine the order of magnitude of $\mathrm{ex}(S_N,C_4)$, the maximum number of edges of a $C_4$-free subgraph of $S_N$.

title: Square-sum orderings avoiding progressions
plain: Line up 1 to N with neighbours summing to squares, and with no three equally spaced positions holding an arithmetic progression.
math: Prove for all large $N$ there is a Hamiltonian path $v_1\dots v_N$ of $S_N$ with no $i<j<k$, $j-i=k-j$, such that $v_i,v_j,v_k$ form an AP.

title: Prime-sum graph is Hamiltonian-connected
plain: Show you can line up 1 to 2n with neighbours summing to primes, starting with any odd number and ending with any even one.
math: Prove for all large $n$ and all odd $a$, even $b$ in $[2n]$, the prime-sum graph on $[2n]$ has a Hamiltonian $a$–$b$ path.

title: Primes in the {5,8} funnel's tree
plain: Look at which starting numbers reach 5 versus 8 first under n ↦ P(n) + P(n+1). Show both happen for a positive fraction of starts.
math: For $f(n)=P(n)+P(n+1)$, prove both $\{n:$ the orbit first meets the cycle at $5\}$ and $\{n:$ first at $8\}$ have positive lower density.

title: Stopping times of the doubling map
plain: For n ↦ 2P(n) + 1, find the typical number of steps to reach its eight-number loop.
math: For $h(n)=2P(n)+1$, prove the number of steps to enter the 8-cycle is $\sim c\log\log n$ for almost all $n$ and find $c$.

title: Distance sets of the spectre tiling
plain: Find how many distinct distances occur between tile centres of the spectre tiling within radius R.
math: Determine the order of growth of $\#\{|x-y|:x,y\in\Lambda_{\mathrm{sp}},|x|,|y|\le R\}$.

title: Isospectral monotiles
plain: Find two different aperiodic monotiles that sound the same as drums.
math: Construct two non-congruent aperiodic monotiles with identical Dirichlet spectra, or prove none exist.

title: Rotation-proof lattice-point-poor shapes
plain: Find the shape in the plane with given area that contains the fewest integer lattice points after any rotation, asymptotically.
math: Determine the convex $K$ of area $A$ minimising $\sup_{\theta}\#(\rho_\theta K\cap\mathbb{Z}^2)$, asymptotically as $A\to\infty$, to second-order term.

title: Moser's worm in the sphere
plain: Find the smallest area region on the unit sphere that can cover every curve of length 1 after a rotation.
math: Determine $\inf\{\sigma(K):K\subset S^2$ covers every rectifiable curve of length $1$ up to $SO(3)\}$ to within $1\%$, and prove the infimum is attained by a set bounded by finitely many circular arcs or show it is not.

title: Equal-area hat dissection
plain: Find the fewest pieces needed to cut a hat tile into pieces that reassemble into a square.
math: Determine the minimal number of polygonal pieces in a scissors-congruence of the unit-edge hat polygon to a square of equal area.

title: Cheeger constant of the sofa
plain: Find the Cheeger constant of Gerver's sofa and show it is transcendental.
