math: Prove $h(G)=\inf_{E\subseteq G}\mathrm{Per}(E)/|E|$ for Gerver's sofa is transcendental.

title: Uniform spanning tree of the square-sum graph
plain: Show a uniformly random spanning tree of the square-sum graph has diameter of order a fixed power of N, and find the exponent.
math: For $T$ a uniform spanning tree of the giant component of $S_N$, prove $\mathrm{diam}(T)=N^{\alpha+o(1)}$ in probability and determine $\alpha$.

title: Percolation threshold of the square-sum graph
plain: Keep each edge of the square-sum graph with probability p. Find the exact threshold for a giant component as N grows.
math: For bond percolation on $S_N$ with $p=c/\sqrt N$, determine $c^*$ such that a component of size $\Theta(N)$ appears w.h.p. iff $c>c^*$.

title: Random greedy square-sum path
plain: Build a path through 1 to N by always stepping to a random unused neighbour summing to a square. Find the expected length.
math: Determine $\lim_N\mathbb{E}[L_N]/N$ for the random greedy path in $S_N$ started at a uniform vertex.

title: Ising with prime couplings
plain: On the integer line, couple spins i and j with strength 1 if i − j is prime. Decide whether there is a phase transition.
math: For the 1D Ising model with $J_{ij}=\mathbf 1[|i-j|\in\mathbb{P}]\,|i-j|^{-2}$, prove a phase transition at finite $\beta_c$ and determine whether the magnetization jumps.

title: Hitting probability for 2P(n)+1 random variant
plain: With probability one half use 2P(n) + 1 and otherwise 2P(n) − 1. Show the walk visits 5 infinitely often.
math: For $X_{t+1}=2P(X_t)\pm1$ with fair signs, prove $X_t=5$ infinitely often almost surely.

title: Random digit deletion
plain: Repeatedly delete a random decimal digit of a number until it is prime or has one digit. Find the probability of ending at a prime from a typical large start.
math: For uniform $n\le x$ and random single-digit deletions, prove $\Pr(\text{the process meets a prime})\to c$ and determine whether $c<1$.

title: Sharp threshold for prime-sum Hamiltonicity
plain: Keep each edge of the prime-sum graph with probability p. Find the threshold for a Hamiltonian cycle.
math: For random subgraphs of the prime-sum graph on $[2n]$ with edge probability $p$, prove the Hamiltonicity threshold is $p^*=(1+o(1))\frac{\log^2 n}{n}$ times an explicit constant, and determine it.

title: Stopping time law for P(n)+P(n+1)
plain: For the map n ↦ P(n) + P(n+1), find the distribution of the number of steps to the {5, 8} loop.
math: Prove the stopping time $\sigma(n)$ of $f(n)=P(n)+P(n+1)$ satisfies $\sigma(n)/\log\log n\to c$ in density, and determine $c$.

title: The shift-3 prime map
plain: Add the largest prime factors of n and n + 3. Every tested start falls into 6, the loop 8 → 13 → 15, or the loop 10 → 18. Prove all do.
math: For $f(n)=P(n)+P(n+3)$, prove every orbit with $n\ge3$ reaches $\{6\}$, $(8,13,15)$ or $(10,18)$.

title: Neighbour factors plus one
plain: Map n to P(n − 1) + P(n + 1) + 1. Tested starts reach 8 → 11 → 9 or 10 → 15. Prove all do.
math: For $f(n)=P(n-1)+P(n+1)+1$, prove every orbit with $n\ge3$ reaches $(8,11,9)$ or $(10,15)$.

title: Four fates of P(n)+P(n+1)+1
plain: Map n to P(n) + P(n+1) + 1. Tested starts reach the fixed point 9 or loops through 6, 19 or 61. Prove these are the only fates.
math: For $f(n)=P(n)+P(n+1)+1$, prove every orbit reaches $\{9\}$, $(6,11,15,8)$, $(19,25)$ or the 4-cycle through $61$.

title: Triple factor map minus two
plain: Map n to P(n) + P(n+1) + P(n+2) − 2. Tested starts reach the fixed points 8 or 33, a 13-step loop through 20, or a 9-step loop through 177. Prove nothing else happens.
math: For $f(n)=P(n)+P(n+1)+P(n+2)-2$, prove every orbit reaches $\{8\}$, $\{33\}$, the 13-cycle through $20$, or the 9-cycle through $177$.

title: Formal verification depth of RH
plain: The Riemann hypothesis now has a Lean proof. Show it cannot be proved in a weak arithmetic like I-Sigma-1 plus exponentiation, or show it can.
math: Decide whether RH (as a $\Pi^0_1$ sentence) is provable in $\mathrm{I}\Sigma_1$, or in $\mathrm{EFA}$.

title: Tileability by the spectre is undecidable for regions with holes
plain: Show deciding whether a finite region with holes can be tiled by spectres is NP-complete.
math: Prove NP-completeness of: given a finite polygonal region $R$ (with holes), decide whether $R$ is tileable by copies of the spectre.

title: Sums of a square and a seven-free prime
plain: Show almost every number is a square plus a prime with no 7 in its decimal digits.
math: Prove the set of $n$ not of the form $m^2+p$ with $p$ prime and $7\notin p$ has density zero.

title: Seven-free factorial-like products
plain: Show n! + 1 contains the digit 7 for all large n.
math: Prove $7\in n!+1$ (decimal) for all sufficiently large $n$.

title: Seven-free square sums of two squares
plain: Show every large seven-free number that is a sum of two squares is a sum of two seven-free squares.
math:
Prove for all large $n$ with $7
otin n$ and $n=a^2+b^2$ solvable, there are $a,b$ with $7
otin a^2$, $7
otin b^2$, $n=a^2+b^2$, or show the exceptional set is infinite.

title: Twin width of square-sum graphs
plain: Show the square-sum graphs do not have bounded twin-width.
math: Prove $\sup_N\mathrm{tww}(S_N)=\infty$.

title: Largest plus smallest neighbour factor
plain: Add the largest prime factor of n to the smallest prime factor of n + 1. Tested starts reach 5 → 7 → 9 or 22 → 34. Prove all do.
math: For $f(n)=P(n)+p(n+1)$, with $p$ the least prime factor, prove every orbit with $n\ge3$ reaches $(5,7,9)$ or $(22,34)$.

title: Sum of prime divisors of neighbours
plain: Add the sum of the distinct prime factors of n to that of n + 1. Tested starts reach 33 or loops through 10, 17, 30 or 107. Prove there is nothing else.

title: Mixed divisor-sum map
plain: Add the sum of distinct prime factors of n to the largest prime factor of n + 1. Tested starts reach 14, 21, or loops through 5, 10, 31 or 82. Prove these are the only fates.

title: Lopsided neighbour map
plain: Map n to P(n) + 2P(n+1). Except for the fixed point 8, every tested start from 3 upward falls into 23 → 29 → 39. Prove this for all starts.
math: For $f(n)=P(n)+2P(n+1)$, prove every orbit with $n\ge3$, $n\ne8$, reaches $(23,29,39)$.

title: The parity-switch prime map
plain: For even n add P(n) and P(n+1); for odd n add P(n) and P(n−1). Every tested start falls into one nine-step loop through 5. Prove all do.
math: For $f(n)=P(n)+P(n+(-1)^n)$, prove every orbit with $n\ge3$ reaches $(5,7,10,16,19,22,34,24,8)$.

title: The shift-6 prime map
plain: Map n to P(n) + P(n+6). Tested starts reach 6 or the loop 8 ↔ 9. Prove all do.
math: For $f(n)=P(n)+P(n+6)$, prove every orbit with $n\ge3$ reaches $\{6\}$ or $(8,9)$.

title: Factor plus next divisor-sum
plain: Map n to P(n) plus the sum of distinct primes dividing n + 1. Every tested start falls into 16 → 19 → 26. Prove all do.
math: For $f(n)=P(n)+\mathrm{sopf}(n+1)$, prove every orbit with $n\ge2$ reaches $(16,19,26)$.

title: Density of the basin of 22 ↔ 34
plain: For n ↦ P(n) + p(n+1), about 6% of tested starts reach the 22 ↔ 34 loop. Show the fraction has a limit and it is positive.
math: For $f(n)=P(n)+p(n+1)$, prove $\lim_{x}\frac1x\#\{n\le x:\text{orbit reaches }(22,34)\}$ exists and is positive.

title: Permanent of the prime-sum matrix
plain: Find the asymptotic count of perfect matchings between odd and even numbers up to 2n whose sums are all prime.
math: Determine $\log\mathrm{per}(M_n)$ to $o(n)$ where $M_n=(\mathbf 1[2i-1+2j\text{ prime}])_{i,j\le n}$.

title: Square-sum matchings count
plain: Count the ways to pair up 1 to N into pairs summing to squares. Find the exponential growth.
math: Determine $\lim_N\frac{\log m(N)}{N}$ (or the right normalisation) for the number $m(N)$ of perfect matchings of $S_N$, $N$ even.

title: Two small factors and one large
plain: Add the smallest prime factors of n and n + 1 to the largest prime factor of n + 2. Every tested start falls into one seven-step loop through 16. Prove all do.
math: For $f(n)=p(n)+p(n+1)+P(n+2)$, prove every orbit with $n\ge2$ reaches $(16,22,28,36,58,66,86)$.

title: The P(n)+P(n+2)+1 map
plain: Map n to P(n) + P(n+2) + 1. Tested starts reach 6, 8, or loops through 9 (12 steps), 19 or 37. Prove these are all.
math: For $f(n)=P(n)+P(n+2)+1$, prove every orbit reaches $\{6\},\{8\}$, the 12-cycle through $9$, $(19,27,33)$ or $(37,51,71,145)$.

title: The P(n)+P(n+2)−1 map
plain: Map n to P(n) + P(n+2) − 1. Tested starts reach 4 or loops of length 18, 11 and 4. Prove these are all.
math: For $f(n)=P(n)+P(n+2)-1$, prove every orbit reaches $\{4\}$, the 18-cycle through $23$, the 11-cycle through $7$, or $(223,227,455,469)$.

title: Unbounded excursions in prime maps
plain: For n ↦ P(n) + P(n+1), show some orbits climb above their starting value by any factor you like.
math: Prove $\sup_n\max_k f^k(n)/n=\infty$ for $f(n)=P(n)+P(n+1)$.

title: Largest-factor subtraction game
plain: From pile n you may remove P(n) stones or any prime smaller than P(n). Characterise the losing positions.
math: For moves $n\to n-q$, $q\in\mathbb{P}$, $q\le P(n)$, prove the P-positions have density zero and determine whether they are infinite.

title: Prime-sum Kayles
plain: Same game on the prime-sum graph: take numbers so that no two taken numbers sum to a prime. Decide who wins.
math: Determine the outcome of the independent-set game on the prime-sum graph on $[N]$ for all large $N$.

title: Large girth subgraphs of S_N
plain: Find the most edges a subgraph of the square-sum graph can have with no cycle shorter than 6.
math: Determine the order of $\mathrm{ex}(S_N,\{C_3,C_4,C_5\})$.

title: Spanning-tree entropy of the spectre tiling
plain: Find the growth rate of the number of spanning trees of large spectre-tiling patches, and show it is not a rational multiple of Catalan's constant.
math: Prove $\lim\frac{\log\tau(G_R)}{|V(G_R)|}=h$ exists for spectre patches and $h/G\notin\mathbb{Q}$, $G$ Catalan's constant.

title: Random square-sum transpositions mixing
plain: Shuffle 1 to N by swapping a random pair that sums to a square. Find the mixing time and show cutoff.
math: For the random walk on $S_N$ (symmetric group) driven by uniform $T$-transpositions, $T$ as above, prove cutoff and determine its location.

title: Prime Markov triples
plain: Show only finitely many Markov triples consist of three primes, or infinitely many.
math: Decide whether infinitely many solutions of $x^2+y^2+z^2=3xyz$ have $x,y,z$ all prime.

title: SOF Collatz orbits are bounded
plain: For the smallest-odd-factor Collatz map, show no orbit runs off to infinity.
math: Prove $\sup_k g^k(n)<\infty$ for every $n$.

title: Sofa for every angle
plain: Find the optimal sofa for a hallway turning by any angle, not just 90°.
math: For every $\theta\in(0,\pi)$, determine the optimal sofa for the width-1 corridor turning by $\theta$.

title: Hat Ising universality
plain: Magnets on a hat tiling should behave at their critical point exactly like magnets on a square grid.
math: Prove the hat-graph Ising model has critical exponents $\beta=1/8$, $\gamma=7/4$, $\nu=1$.

title: Finite simple groups in Lean
plain: Turn the classification of finite simple groups into one computer-checked proof.
math: Formalize the classification of finite simple groups in Lean 4.

title: Cube-sum paths
plain: Arrange 1 to N in a line so neighbours add to perfect cubes, for every large N.
math: Prove $C_N$ has a Hamiltonian path for all sufficiently large $N$.

title: Alternating prime residues
plain: Find ten consecutive primes whose remainders mod 4 alternate 1, 3, 1, 3, …, and infinitely many such runs.
math: Prove infinitely many $n$ with $p_{n+i}\equiv 2+(-1)^{i}\pmod 4$ for $0\le i<10$.

title: Largest-factor climbs
plain: Show infinitely many starts climb above their own square before falling.
math: Prove $\max_k f^k(n)>n^2$ for infinitely many $n$.

title: Counting Prime Nim losses
plain: Show the losing positions of Prime Nim thin out at a precise power rate.
math: Prove $|L\cap[1,x]|=x^{\alpha+o(1)}$ for some $\alpha$ and compute it.

title: Prime Nim in polylog time
plain: Decide whether a Prime Nim pile is losing in time polynomial in its number of digits.
math: Give an algorithm deciding $G(n)=0$ in time $(\log n)^{O(1)}$, or prove none exists under a standard assumption.

title: Primes a² + b⁴ with prime inputs
plain: Show infinitely many primes are a square of a prime plus a fourth power of a prime.
math: Prove infinitely many primes of the form $p^2+q^4$ with $p,q$ prime.

title: Primes x² + y³ with prime inputs
plain: Show infinitely many primes are a square of a prime plus a cube of a prime.
math: Prove infinitely many primes of the form $p^2+q^3$ with $p,q$ prime.

title: Doubly smooth neighbours
plain: Find infinitely many primes whose two neighbours have only small prime factors.
math: Prove infinitely many primes $p$ with $P(p-1),P(p+1)\le p^{0.1}$.

title: High-dimensional sofa
plain: How does the best sofa's volume grow in an n-dimensional corridor?
math: Determine the asymptotics in $n$ of the optimal volume in the $n$-dimensional right-angled corridor of unit cross-section.

title: Ambidextrous 3D sofa
plain: Find the largest solid that can turn either left or right at the end of a square pipe.
math: Maximize volume over solids admissible for both the left and right turns of the $1\times1$ corridor.

title: Polykite structure theorem
plain: Classify every shape of up to 20 kites: tiles periodically, tiles only aperiodically, or fails within a few layers.
math: Prove each polykite with $\le20$ kites either tiles periodically, tiles only aperiodically, or has Heesch number $\le10$.

title: Hard-hat transition
plain: Show the gas of non-overlapping hats freezes abruptly at some density.
math: Prove the hard-hat lattice gas has a first-order phase transition in the activity.

title: Sparse Keller maps
plain: List every Jacobian-conjecture counterexample in 3D built from at most 12 monomials in total, up to symmetry.
math: Classify all non-invertible Keller maps $\mathbb{C}^3\to\mathbb{C}^3$ whose three components together have at most 12 monomials, up to affine changes of coordinates.

title: Analytic hyperoperations
plain: Build one smooth family of operations from addition up through exponentiation that is analytic in all inputs.
math: Construct $a[s]b$, real-analytic in $(s,a,b)$ for $s\in[1,3]$, $a>1$, $b>0$, satisfying the recursion law and matching $+,\times,\uparrow$.

title: Time-independent force
plain: Make viscous fluid blow up with a push that never changes in time.
math: Construct smooth compactly supported time-independent $f$ such that 3D Navier–Stokes from rest blows up in finite time.

title: Stable blow-up
plain: Show the 2026 Navier–Stokes blow-up still happens after any tiny change to the setup.
math: Prove the 2026 forced blow-up is stable under small smooth perturbations of $(u_0,f)$ in a suitable topology.

title: Square-sum pancyclicity
plain: Show the square-sum graph has cycles of every possible length.
math: Prove $S_N$ is pancyclic on its 2-connected core for all large $N$.

title: Prime-speed lonely runners
plain: Prove the lonely runner conjecture when every speed is a prime number.
math: For distinct primes $p_1,\dots,p_n$, prove $\sup_t\min_i\|tp_i\|\ge\frac1{n+1}$.

title: Counting minimal Sudokus
plain: How many uniquely solvable Sudokus with no removable clue exist, as the board grows?
math: Find the asymptotics of the number of minimal uniquely solvable $n^2\times n^2$ puzzles.

title: Gomoku on hats
plain: Prove the first player wins five-in-a-row on an infinite board of hat tiles.
math: Prove the first player has a winning strategy in the 5-in-a-row game on the hat adjacency graph (rows = geodesic paths).

title: Hyperoperation Goodstein
plain: A Goodstein-style sequence using hyperoperations always ends, but ordinary arithmetic cannot prove it.
math: Define base-change on hereditary hyperoperation normal forms; prove the sequences terminate and termination is unprovable in PA.

title: Unique 3D sofa
plain: Show the best solid for a square pipe is unique up to moving it.
math: Prove the optimizer for the $1\times1$ square corridor is unique up to rigid motion.

title: Vorticity growth in a hat
plain: Fluid in a hat-shaped container should develop sharper and sharper swirls near its corners.
math: For 2D Euler in the hat polygon, prove $\|\nabla\omega(t)\|_\infty$ grows double exponentially for some smooth initial data.

title: Fluid in a box blows up
plain: Show viscous fluid in a closed box with sticky walls can blow up under a smooth push.
math: Construct smooth $f$ such that 3D Navier–Stokes with no-slip in the unit cube blows up in finite time.

title: Toroidal Othello
plain: Who wins Othello on an 8 × 8 board that wraps around?
math: Weakly solve Othello on $\mathbb{Z}_8^2$ with standard initial position.

title: Infinitely many prime squared squares
plain: Show there are infinitely many perfect squared squares whose pieces all have prime sides.
math: Prove infinitely many perfect squared squares with all component sides prime.

title: Divisor-balanced primes
plain: Show infinitely many primes p have p − 1 and p + 1 with the same number of divisors.
math: Prove infinitely many primes $p$ with $d(p-1)=d(p+1)$.

title: Reverse-square cycles
plain: Square and reverse the digits, repeatedly. Show there are infinitely many different loops.
math: Prove $R(n)=\operatorname{rev}(n^2)$ has infinitely many distinct cycles.

title: Chen with no sevens
plain: Show infinitely many seven-free primes p have p + 2 a product of at most two seven-free primes.
math: Prove infinitely many 7-free primes $p$ with $p+2=q_1q_2$ or $q_1$, all $q_i$ prime and 7-free.

title: Nodal domains of the hat drum
plain: Count the regions a hat-shaped drum splits into when vibrating at high frequencies.
math: For Dirichlet eigenfunctions on the hat polygon, prove $\limsup N(\varphi_k)/k=c<1$ and compute $c$.

title: Hat billiard scarring
plain: Show high-frequency waves in a hat-shaped room do not spread out evenly.
math: Prove quantum unique ergodicity fails for the hat polygon: some subsequence of eigenfunctions has a non-uniform limit measure.

title: Homogenized wildfire
plain: Fire spreads through random patches of two fuel types. Show it has a definite average speed and compute it.
math: For the eikonal equation with i.i.d. two-valued speed on a lattice, prove homogenization and give the effective speed in closed form.

title: Galois groups of Keller fibers
plain: Find the symmetry group of the preimages of a point under the 2026 Keller maps.
math: Compute the Galois group of the generic fiber of Gallagher's degree-$n$ Keller family for each $n\ge3$.

title: Palindromic Carmichael numbers
plain: Show infinitely many Carmichael numbers read the same backwards.
math: Prove there are infinitely many Carmichael numbers that are decimal palindromes.

title: Shrink to fit
plain: Find the largest size such that every convex shape no wider than that, measured end to end, gets around the corner.
math: Find the largest $d$ such that every planar convex body of diameter $\le d$ is admissible in the width-1 right-angled corridor.

title: Symmetric sofa
plain: Find the best sofa that is symmetric under a half-turn.
math: Maximize area over centrally symmetric sets admissible in the width-1 right-angled corridor.

title: Convex sofa
plain: Find the best convex sofa.
math: Maximize area over convex sets admissible in the width-1 right-angled corridor.

title: Unattained hyperbolic sofa
plain: In strongly curved hyperbolic space the best sofa might not exist. Show when the maximum is never reached.
math: Find $\kappa_0$ such that for curvature $-\kappa<-\kappa_0$ the hyperbolic sofa supremum is not attained.

title: Squares on a sphere
plain: Every closed curve on a sphere should pass through the corners of a spherical square.
math: Prove every Jordan curve on $S^2$ inscribes a spherical quadrilateral with equal sides and equal angles.

title: Cross-polytopes in 4D
plain: Every 4D convex body should have the corners of a regular cross-polytope on its boundary.
math: Prove every convex body in $\mathbb{R}^4$ has an inscribed regular cross-polytope.

title: One firefighter on hats
plain: Can a single firefighter per turn contain every fire on a hat tiling?
math: Decide whether one protected vertex per turn contains any single-vertex fire on the hat graph.

title: Prime and square neighbours
plain: Order all positive integers so neighbours add to a prime and numbers two apart add to a square.
math: Decide whether there is a bijection $\pi:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ with $\pi_i+\pi_{i+1}$ prime and $\pi_i+\pi_{i+2}$ square for all $i$.

title: Prime-graceful forests
plain: Label any forest so the edge differences are exactly the first m primes.
math: Prove every forest with $m$ edges has an injective $\ell:V\to\mathbb{Z}_{\ge0}$ whose edge differences are $\{p_1,\dots,p_m\}$.

title: Carmichael numbers with prime digit sum
plain: Show infinitely many Carmichael numbers have a digit sum that is prime.
math: Prove infinitely many Carmichael numbers $n$ with $s_{10}(n)$ prime.

title: Hat tiling Lee–Yang zeros
plain: For magnets on a hat tiling, show the complex zeros of the partition function pinch the real axis at exactly one point.
math: Prove the Lee–Yang zeros of the ferromagnetic Ising model on growing hat patches accumulate on the positive real temperature axis only at $\beta_c$.

title: Square-sum expansion
plain: Show the square-sum graph (on its large connected piece) is a good expander.
math: Prove the giant component of $S_N$ has spectral gap at least $(\log N)^{-C}$.

title: Doubled-twin sieve upper bound
plain: Bound the number of doubled-twin quadruples up to x by the predicted count times at most 3.
math: Prove $\#\{p\le x: p,p+2,2p+1,2p+3\text{ prime}\}\le(3+o(1))\,\mathfrak{S}x/\log^4x$, with $\mathfrak S$ the singular series.

title: Largest-factor cycles
plain: Find every loop of the largest-factor Collatz map.
math: Prove every periodic orbit of $f(n)=n/2$ (even), $P(3n+1)$ (odd) lies in an explicit finite list, and give it.

title: Sofa with a rotating door
plain: A door at the corner swings shut as you move. Find the largest shape that still gets through.
math: Determine the maximal area of a set passing the width-1 right-angled corridor while the region $\{x>1,y>1\}$ moves by a prescribed rotating half-line barrier.

title: Hyperoperation fixed points
plain: In any natural real-rank hyperoperation family, show the rank at which 2 ∘ 2 stops being 4 is not a whole number.
math: For the unique analytic family $a[s]b$ satisfying the recursion and log-convexity in $s$, prove $\{s: 2[s]2=4\}$ is exactly $[1,\infty)\cap$ an explicit closed set and determine whether it is an interval.

title: Graceful forests with one big tree
plain: A forest with c trees and m edges is graceful-forest labelled if its vertices get the labels 0 to m + c − 1 with all edge differences distinct. Show this works whenever there are at least two trees and one of them holds more than half the edges.
math: Prove every forest with $m$ edges and $c\ge2$ components, one of which has more than $m/2$ edges, has a bijection $V\to\{0,\dots,m+c-1\}$ with all $|\ell(u)-\ell(v)|$, $uv\in E$, distinct.

title: Keller maps with integer fibers
plain: Show no Jacobian-conjecture counterexample with integer coefficients is injective on integer points but not invertible.
math: Prove every Keller map $F\in\mathbb{Z}[x,y,z]^3$ injective on $\mathbb{Z}^3$ is a polynomial automorphism of $\mathbb{C}^3$.

title: Fire on a random hat patch
plain: Remove each hat tile with some probability. Find the exact point where a fire can no longer burn forever.
math: Prove the site-percolation threshold of the hat tiling exists as a single sharp value and bound it within $10^{-4}$.

title: Emirp twins
plain: Show infinitely many twin-prime pairs exist where both reverse to primes, assuming only standard sieve bounds plus one level-of-distribution hypothesis.
math: Assuming Elliott–Halberstam, prove infinitely many $p$ with $p,p+2,\operatorname{rev}(p),\operatorname{rev}(p+2)$ prime among bounded gaps of tuples $(p,p+h)$, $h\le H$ explicit.

title: Seven-free Goldbach
plain: Show almost every even number is a sum of two primes that have no digit 7.
math: Prove all but $o(x)$ even $n\le x$ are sums of two 7-free primes.

title: Hat mixing time
plain: Randomly flip local patches of a hat tiling. Show it mixes in polynomial time.
math: For local-move Glauber dynamics on hat tilings of an $L\times L$ region, prove mixing time $L^{O(1)}$.

title: Tetris on a cylinder
plain: When the board wraps left to right, can a player survive forever against any piece sequence?
math: Decide whether a player can survive indefinitely in a width-10 cylindrical Tetris well against adversarial piece sequences with 1-piece preview.

title: Sofa in curved space with a corner
plain: On a cone-shaped surface the hallway corner is the cone point. Find the best sofa.
math: For the width-1 corridor on a flat cone of angle $\alpha$ with the inner corner at the apex, find the optimal sofa area as a function of $\alpha$.

title: Joint digit sums of primes
plain: Show infinitely many primes have a prime digit sum in base 2 and in base 10 at the same time.
math: Prove infinitely many primes $p$ have $s_2(p)$ and $s_{10}(p)$ both prime.

title: Squares of seven-free primes
plain: Show infinitely many primes have no digit 7 in themselves or in their squares.
math: Prove infinitely many primes $p$ with neither $p$ nor $p^2$ containing the decimal digit 7.

title: Irrational prime weights
plain: Add up 1/(p·2^p) over all primes p. Show the total is irrational.
math: Prove $\sum_{p}\frac{1}{p\,2^{p}}$ is irrational.

title: Prime-indexed seven-free primes
plain: List the primes in order. Show infinitely many seven-free primes sit at a prime position in that list.
math: Prove infinitely many primes $p_q$ with $q$ prime and $p_q$ free of the decimal digit 7.

title: Square-sum edge-Hamiltonian
plain: Show every edge of the square-sum graph lies on a loop through all of 1 to N, for large N.
math: Prove that for all large $N$, every edge of $S_N$ lies on a Hamiltonian cycle of $S_N$.

title: Square-sum clique minors
plain: Find the largest complete graph that can be formed by contracting parts of the square-sum graph.
math: Determine the order of growth of the Hadwiger number $h(S_N)$.

title: Prime-sum Hamiltonian count
plain: Count the ways to arrange 1 to 2n in a circle so neighbours sum to primes. Find the growth rate.
math: Let $H_n$ count Hamiltonian cycles of the prime-sum graph on $[2n]$. Prove $\log H_n=(1+o(1))\,c\,n\log n$ and find $c$.

title: Turán density with a twist
plain: Same question for a seven-vertex configuration of five triples arranged around a central triple.

title: Seven-free Carmichael quotients
plain: Show infinitely many Carmichael numbers n have n − 1 seven-free.
math: Prove infinitely many Carmichael numbers $n$ such that $n-1$ has no decimal digit 7.

title: Lonely runners with square speeds
plain: Prove the lonely runner conjecture when all speeds are perfect squares.
math: For distinct positive integers $a_1,\dots,a_n$, prove $\sup_t\min_i\|ta_i^2\|\ge\frac1{n+1}$.

title: 4p+1 maximal climbs
plain: Show the 4p + 1 prime map can climb arbitrarily high above its starting point before falling into its loop.
math: Prove $\sup_p \max_k P_4^k(p)/p=\infty$, where $P_4(p)=P(4p+1)$.

title: Antiferromagnetic hats
plain: Colour hat tiles up or down to minimise same-colour neighbours. The hat graph has odd cycles, so some frustration is unavoidable. Compute the ground-state entropy exactly.
math: For the antiferromagnetic Ising model on the hat graph, prove the zero-temperature entropy per tile exists, is positive, and compute it in closed form.

title: Potts transition on hats
plain: Show the q-state Potts model on the hat tiling has a discontinuous transition for large q, and a continuous one for q = 2.
math: Prove the $q$-state Potts model on the hat graph has a first-order transition for all $q\ge q_0$ and a continuous one for $q=2$; find the least such $q_0$.

title: Prime-sum labelling of balanced trees
plain: Label a tree with 1 to n so every edge sums to a prime. Parity forces the two sides of the tree to be balanced. Show balance is enough, for large n.
math: Prove every tree on $n\ge n_0$ vertices whose bipartition classes have sizes $\lceil n/2\rceil,\lfloor n/2\rfloor$ admits a bijection $V\to[n]$ with all edge sums prime.

title: Hyperdissipative forced blow-up
plain: Fluids with extra strong viscosity never blow up above a known threshold. Show forced blow-up still happens just below it.
math: For $\partial_tu+(u\cdot\nabla)u+\nabla p=-(-\Delta)^{\alpha}u+f$ on $\mathbb{R}^3$, construct smooth compactly supported $f$ giving finite-time blow-up from rest for every $\alpha<5/4$.

title: Hat tilings of convex regions
plain: Show no convex polygon can be tiled exactly by hats.
math: Prove no convex polygon is a finite union of interior-disjoint congruent hats (reflections allowed), or exhibit one.

title: Lattice gauge on the hat
plain: Show the Z/2 lattice gauge theory on a hat-tiled surface times a line has a deconfinement transition.
math: For $\mathbb{Z}_2$ lattice gauge theory on the 3D cell complex $\mathrm{hat}\times\mathbb{Z}$, prove the Wilson loop changes from area law to perimeter law at a single critical coupling.

title: Prime cubes with one shift
plain: Show infinitely many quadruples of primes satisfy x³ + y³ = z³ + w³ + 1.
math: Prove infinitely many prime solutions $(x,y,z,w)$ of $x^3+y^3=z^3+w^3+1$.

title: Prime points on a quartic threefold
plain: Count prime solutions of x⁴ + y⁴ + z⁴ = w⁴ + 2 up to size X, and find the asymptotic.
math: Find the asymptotic number of prime 4-tuples $\le X$ with $x^4+y^4+z^4=w^4+2$, or prove there are finitely many.

title: Sidon sets of hat tiles
plain: Pick hat tiles so all pairwise displacement vectors are distinct. How many can fit in a region of n tiles?
math: Determine the asymptotics of the maximum size of $A\subseteq B_L$ (hat-tiled $L$-ball, tile centres) with all differences $a-a'$, $a\ne a'$, distinct.

title: Sofa constant digits
plain: Show the digits of Gerver's sofa area do not end in a repeating pattern in base 2 either, and give an explicit irrationality measure bound.
math: Prove $\mu_G$ is irrational with irrationality measure $\le 100$.

title: Hat Ising critical line
plain: Ising models on a hat tiling and its dual should be exactly related at their critical points. Prove the duality relation holds rigorously.
math: For the ferromagnetic Ising model on the hat graph $G$ and its planar dual $G^*$, prove $\sinh(2\beta_c(G))\sinh(2\beta_c(G^*))=1$.

title: Hat Hofstadter at golden flux
plain: Thread a magnetic flux through each hat tile equal to the golden ratio. Show the resulting energy spectrum is a zero-measure Cantor set.
math: For the magnetic tight-binding Hamiltonian on the hat graph with flux $\phi=(\sqrt5-1)/2$ per kite, prove $\sigma(H)$ is a Cantor set of Lebesgue measure zero.

title: Blow-up near a wall
plain: Show the 2026 forced blow-up mechanism also works in a half-space with no-slip wall, with the singularity on the wall.
math: Construct smooth compactly supported $f$ such that Navier–Stokes in $\mathbb{R}^3_+$ with no-slip, from rest, blows up in finite time at a boundary point.

title: Unit distances in three dimensions after 2026
plain: The 2026 number-field idea beat Erdős in the plane. Adapt it to unit distances among points on a sphere in 3D.
math: Prove there are $n$-point sets on the unit sphere $S^2$ with $\ge n^{1+c}$ pairs at distance $1$, for some $c>0$ and infinitely many $n$.

title: Lonely runner gap for the first n primes
plain: For the first n primes as speeds, find the actual loneliness gap asymptotically.
math: Determine the asymptotics of $\delta_n=\sup_t\min_{i\le n}\|tp_i\|$ as $n\to\infty$.

title: Hat dominoes freeze
plain: Random domino-style pairings of hat tiles inside a large region with a fixed boundary develop a frozen outer zone. Find the shape of the boundary between frozen and random regions.
math: For uniform perfect matchings of the hat graph on regions $L\cdot\Omega$, prove an arctic curve exists and identify it for $\Omega$ a regular hexagon.

title: Spectre billiards ergodic
plain: Billiards inside a spectre-shaped room with curved walls should be chaotic. Prove the billiard flow is ergodic.
math: Prove the billiard flow in the spectre (with its circular-arc edges) is ergodic with respect to Liouville measure.

title: Square Nim from both ends
plain: Two piles; a move removes a square from one pile or the same square from both. Find the losing positions' asymptotic density.
math: For moves $(a,b)\to(a-k^2,b),(a,b-k^2),(a-k^2,b-k^2)$, prove $\#\{(a,b)\in[N]^2:\mathcal P\}=N^{1+\theta+o(1)}$ and find $\theta$.

title: Seven-free values of n²+1
plain: Show infinitely many n make n² + 1 a prime with no digit 7, or at least a product of two such primes.
math: Prove infinitely many $n$ with $n^2+1=q_1q_2$, $q_i$ primes free of the digit 7.

title: Prime Nim values stay small
plain: Prime Nim's Grundy values grow incredibly slowly. Show they are at most a constant times log n.
math: For the subtraction game with prime moves, prove $G(n)=O(\log n)$.

title: Long progressions of seven-free primes
plain: Show the seven-free primes contain arbitrarily long arithmetic progressions.
math: Prove for every $k$ there are $k$-term arithmetic progressions consisting of primes with no decimal digit 7.

title: Seven-free Gaussian primes
plain: Show infinitely many primes a² + b² have both a and b free of the digit 7.
math: Prove infinitely many primes $a^2+b^2$ with $a,b$ positive integers free of the decimal digit 7.

title: Linnik for seven-free primes
plain: Show the smallest seven-free prime in an arithmetic progression is at most a fixed power of the modulus.
math: Prove there is $C$ such that for every $q$ and $(a,q)=1$ (with $10\nmid q$-compatibility conditions) there is a 7-free prime $p\equiv a\ (q)$, $p\le q^C$.

title: Monochromatic square-sum triangles, many colours
plain: Colour the positive integers with any finite number of colours. Show there are always three numbers of one colour whose pairwise sums are all squares.
math: Prove that for every $r$ and every $r$-colouring of $\mathbb{N}$ there are distinct $a,b,c$ of one colour with $a+b,a+c,b+c$ all perfect squares.

title: Keller monodromy is everything
plain: Show every symmetric group appears as the hidden symmetry group of the fibres of some 3D Jacobian-conjecture counterexample.
math: Prove that for each $n\ge3$ there is a non-invertible Keller map $\mathbb{C}^3\to\mathbb{C}^3$ of geometric degree $n$ whose generic monodromy group is $S_n$.

title: Hat tiling heat kernel constant
plain: For a random walk on a hat tiling, find the exact constant in the return probability.
math: Prove $p_{2n}(o,o)\sim\frac{c(o)}{n}$ on the hat graph and show $\frac1{|B_R|}\sum_{o\in B_R}c(o)\to c$ with $c=\frac{\bar d}{2\pi\sqrt{\det\Sigma}}$, computing $\Sigma$ in closed form.

title: Four-term square-sum chains in primes
plain: Find infinitely many chains of four primes where each neighbouring pair sums to a square.
math: Prove infinitely many 4-tuples of primes $p_1,p_2,p_3,p_4$ with $p_i+p_{i+1}$ a square for $i=1,2,3$.

title: Hat quasicrystal Ising universality, bond-disordered
plain: Randomly weaken some bonds in the hat Ising model. Show the critical behaviour still matches the clean 2D Ising class up to logs.
math: For the random-bond ferromagnetic Ising model on the hat graph with i.i.d. couplings in $[1,1+\varepsilon]$, prove the specific heat diverges at most as $\log\log|t|^{-1}$ near $T_c$ for small $\varepsilon$.

title: The spectre is not spectral
plain: Show the spectre, a curved tile that cannot tile by translations, has no orthogonal basis of exponentials, as Fuglede's conjecture predicts.
math: Prove there is no $\Lambda\subset\mathbb{R}^2$ such that $\{e^{2\pi i\lambda\cdot x}\}_{\lambda\in\Lambda}$ is an orthogonal basis of $L^2$ of the spectre domain.

title: First appearances in Prime Nim
plain: The smallest pile with Grundy value k in Prime Nim grows extremely fast. Show it grows at least exponentially in k.
math: Let $a(k)=\min\{n:G(n)=k\}$ for the prime subtraction game. Prove $a(k)\ge e^{ck}$ for some $c>0$ and all $k$ for which $a(k)$ exists.

title: Rational fibres of the Alpöge map
plain: The 2026 Jacobian counterexample sends three rational points to one point. Show infinitely many rational target points have three rational preimages.
math: For Alpöge's Keller map $F:\mathbb{Q}^3\to\mathbb{Q}^3$, prove $\{y\in\mathbb{Q}^3:|F^{-1}(y)\cap\mathbb{Q}^3|=3\}$ is Zariski dense in $\mathbb{A}^3$.

title: Seven-free squares
plain: Count the numbers up to x whose square has no digit 7. Show the count matches the random-digit prediction.

title: Weyl remainder for the hat drum
plain: Count the vibration frequencies of a hat-shaped drum below a threshold. Find the true size of the error after the two leading terms.
math: For the Dirichlet Laplacian on the hat polygon, prove $N(\lambda)=\frac{|\Omega|}{4\pi}\lambda-\frac{|\partial\Omega|}{4\pi}\sqrt\lambda+O(\lambda^{\theta})$ and determine the optimal $\theta$.

title: Few periodic points of square-plus-one
plain: Count the numbers up to X that lie on a loop of the square-plus-one map. Show there are very few.
math: Prove $\#\{n\le X: Q^k(n)=n\text{ for some }k\ge1\}=X^{o(1)}$, where $Q(n)=P(n^2+1)$.

title: Finitely many loops for affine prime maps
plain: For fixed a and b, show the prime map p ↦ largest prime factor of ap + b has only finitely many loops.
math: Prove that for all integers $a\ge2$, $b\ge1$, the map $p\mapsto P(ap+b)$ on primes has finitely many periodic orbits.

title: Missing digits in two bases
plain: Show infinitely many primes have no digit 9 in base 10 and no digit 10 in base 11 at the same time.
math: Prove infinitely many primes whose base-10 expansion avoids the digit 9 and whose base-11 expansion avoids the digit 10.

title: The last even loss in Prime Nim
plain: In Prime Nim almost every losing pile size is odd. The only even ones found are 0, 10, 34, 100 and 310. Prove there are no more.
math: For the subtraction game with prime moves, prove $\{n \text{ even}: G(n)=0\}=\{0,10,34,100,310\}$.

title: Largest factor of n²+1 mod 8
plain: The largest prime factor of n² + 1 is always 1 or 5 mod 8 (or 2). Show both happen equally often.
math: Prove $\#\{n\le x: P(n^2+1)\equiv1\ (8)\}\sim\#\{n\le x:P(n^2+1)\equiv5\ (8)\}\sim x/2$.

title: Largest factor of shifted primes mod 4
plain: For primes p, look at the largest prime factor of p − 1. Show it is 1 mod 4 exactly half the time.
math: Prove $\#\{p\le x: P(p-1)\equiv1\ (4)\}\sim\tfrac12\pi(x)$.

title: Conformal radius of the hat
plain: Map a disc conformally onto the hat so the centre goes to the hat's centroid. Show the scale factor is transcendental.
math: Prove the conformal radius of the hat polygon at its centroid is transcendental.

title: Spanning trees inside the prime-sum graph
plain: Show every balanced tree of bounded degree on 2n vertices can be laid out on 1 to 2n so all its edges sum to primes.
math: Prove that for every $\Delta$ there is $n_0$ such that every tree on $2n\ge n_0$ vertices with maximum degree $\le\Delta$ and bipartition classes of size $n$ is a spanning subgraph of the prime-sum graph on $[2n]$.

title: Spanning trees inside the square-sum graph
plain: Show every tree of maximum degree 3 on N vertices fits inside the square-sum graph on 1 to N.
math: Prove every tree on $N\ge N_0$ vertices with maximum degree $\le3$ is a spanning subgraph of $S_N$.

title: AKLT on the hat
plain: Show the AKLT quantum spin model placed on a hat tiling has an energy gap above its ground state.
math: For the AKLT Hamiltonian on the vertex graph of a hat tiling (spin $d(v)/2$ at vertex $v$), prove a uniform spectral gap on finite patches.

title: Digit-restricted Liouville
plain: Show the Liouville function has no bias on seven-free numbers in short intervals.
math: Prove $\sum_{x<n\le x+H,\ 7\notin n}\lambda(n)=o(\#\{x<n\le x+H:7\notin n\})$ for almost all $x\le X$, with $H=X^{0.1}$.

title: Square-plus-one orbits avoid small primes
plain: Show that infinitely many starting numbers have square-plus-one sequences that never fall below their start.
math: Prove infinitely many $n$ with $Q^k(n)\ge n$ for all $k\ge1$.

title: Prime cycles of all lengths
plain: Show that for every length L, some map p ↦ largest prime factor of ap + b has a loop of exactly length L.
math: Prove that for every $L\ge1$ there are $a,b\ge1$ such that $p\mapsto P(ap+b)$ has a periodic orbit of exact length $L$.

title: Spectre hard hexagons
plain: Show the hard-core gas on the spectre tiling has exactly one phase transition, at a single sharp activity.
math: Prove the hard-core model on the spectre adjacency graph has a unique critical activity $\lambda_c$ with uniqueness for $\lambda<\lambda_c$ and non-uniqueness for $\lambda>\lambda_c$.

title: Largest factor ratio of consecutive primes
plain: For consecutive primes p < q, compare the largest prime factors of p − 1 and q − 1. Show each is larger half the time.

title: Seven-free primes in Piatetski-Shapiro sequences
plain: Show infinitely many primes of the form ⌊n^1.1⌋ have no digit 7.
math: Prove infinitely many primes $\lfloor n^{1.1}\rfloor$ free of the decimal digit 7.

title: Quasi-independence of square-plus-one steps
plain: Show the largest prime factors of n² + 1 and (n + 1)² + 1 are nearly independent in size.

title: Prime Nim's mod-3 bias
plain: Losing pile sizes in Prime Nim are about three times as likely to be 1 mod 3 as 0 mod 3. Find the exact limiting proportions.
math: For the prime subtraction game, prove the limits $\lim_x\#\{n\le x:G(n)=0,\ n\equiv r\ (3)\}/\#\{n\le x:G(n)=0\}$ exist for $r=0,1,2$, and determine them.

title: Square losses in Prime Nim
plain: Many perfect squares (1, 9, 25, 49, 100, 121, …) are losing Prime Nim positions. Show there are infinitely many.
math: Prove infinitely many perfect squares $k^2$ satisfy $G(k^2)=0$ in the prime subtraction game.

title: Progressions of Prime Nim losses
plain: Show the losing positions of Prime Nim contain arbitrarily long arithmetic progressions.
math: Prove $\{n:G(n)=0\}$ contains $k$-term arithmetic progressions for every $k$.

title: Bombieri–Vinogradov for seven-free primes in base 10
plain: Show seven-free primes are well distributed in arithmetic progressions on average over moduli up to x^θ, for some θ > 0, in base 10.
math: Prove there is $\theta>0$ such that $\sum_{q\le x^\theta}\max_{(a,q)=1}\big|\pi_7(x;q,a)-\frac{\pi_7(x)}{\varphi(q)}\big|\ll_A \pi_7(x)(\log x)^{-A}$, where $\pi_7$ counts 7-free primes (moduli coprime to 10).

title: Increasing square-plus-one factors
plain: Among the largest prime factors of n² + 1 for n up to N, find the longest strictly increasing subsequence.
math: Determine $\theta$ with $L(N)=N^{\theta+o(1)}$, where $L(N)$ is the longest strictly increasing subsequence of $(P(n^2+1))_{n\le N}$.

title: Density of Grundy value one in Prime Nim
plain: Show the pile sizes with Grundy value exactly 1 in Prime Nim have a definite density, and that it is positive.
math: For the prime subtraction game, prove $\lim_x\frac1x\#\{n\le x:G(n)=1\}$ exists and is positive.

title: Two long loops
plain: Replace n by P(3n + 1) + P(n). Every tested start ends in one of two long loops, through 46 or through 80. Prove there are no others.
math: Prove every orbit of $n\mapsto P(3n+1)+P(n)$ on $n\ge2$ enters the 9-cycle through 46 or the 7-cycle through 80.

title: Neighbours' largest factors
plain: Replace n by P(n − 1) + P(n + 1). Every tested start ends at 5 or in one of three loops, of lengths 11, 18 and 4. Prove there is nothing else.
math: Prove every orbit of $n\mapsto P(n-1)+P(n+1)$ on $n\ge3$ enters $\{5\}$, the 11-cycle through 8, the 18-cycle through 24, or $(224,228,456,470)$.

title: Gerver's constant has unbounded partial quotients
plain: Show the continued fraction of Gerver's sofa area contains arbitrarily large terms.
math: Prove the continued fraction expansion of $\mu_G\approx2.2195$ has unbounded partial quotients.

title: Every binary block in Gerver's constant
plain: Show every finite string of 0s and 1s appears somewhere in the binary expansion of Gerver's sofa area.
math: Prove the binary expansion of $\mu_G$ is disjunctive (contains every finite word).

title: Prime continued fractions
plain: Consider real numbers whose continued fraction terms are all prime. Show the fractal dimension of this set is transcendental.
math: Let $E=\{x\in(0,1): \text{all partial quotients of }x\text{ are prime}\}$. Prove $\dim_H E$ is transcendental.

title: Five squares of seven-free primes
plain: Show every large number of the right residue is a sum of five squares of primes without the digit 7.
math: Prove every sufficiently large $n\equiv5\pmod{24}$ is $p_1^2+\dots+p_5^2$ with all $p_i$ prime and free of the decimal digit 7.

title: Large prime factors of 2^n + 3^n
plain: Show the largest prime factor of 2^n + 3^n grows faster than n².
math: Prove $P(2^n+3^n)/n^2\to\infty$.

title: Infinite monochromatic square-sum paths
plain: Colour the positive integers red and blue. Show there is always an infinite increasing sequence of one colour in which every two consecutive terms sum to a perfect square.
math: Prove every 2-colouring of $\mathbb{N}$ admits $a_1<a_2<\cdots$ of one colour with $a_i+a_{i+1}$ a perfect square for all $i$.

title: Is Prime Nim's losing set definable?
plain: Add the set of Prime Nim losing positions to the arithmetic of addition. Is the resulting theory decidable?
math: Decide whether the first-order theory of $(\mathbb{N},+,L)$ is decidable, where $L=\{n:G(n)=0\}$ for the prime subtraction game.

title: Packing density of Gerver's sofa
plain: Find the densest way to pack copies of Gerver's sofa shape in the plane, and show the density is not a rational multiple of an algebraic number.
math: Let $\delta_G$ be the translative-and-rotational packing density of Gerver's sofa. Prove $\delta_G\notin\overline{\mathbb{Q}}$.

title: Prime-digit continued fractions in arithmetic progressions
plain: Show there are infinitely many quadratic irrationals all of whose continued fraction digits are prime, in each real quadratic field.
math: Prove for every real quadratic field $K$ there are infinitely many $\alpha\in K$ with purely periodic continued fraction expansion having all partial quotients prime.

title: Ising model on the spectre tiling
plain: Find the exact critical temperature of the Ising model on the spectre tiling graph, and prove the interfaces converge to SLE(3).
math: For the nearest-neighbour Ising model on the spectre-tiling vertex graph, determine $\beta_c$ and prove critical interfaces converge to $\mathrm{SLE}_3$.

title: Doubled prime map with a 1231 loop
plain: Map n to twice its largest prime factor plus the largest prime factor of n + 1. Starts below 150,000 reach either a five-step loop through 93 or a three-step loop through 1231. Prove there are no other fates.

title: Largest prime factor of 2^n + n
plain: Show the largest prime factor of 2^n + n tends to infinity faster than any fixed multiple of n.
math: Prove $P(2^n+n)/n\to\infty$.

title: Largest prime factor of n^n + 1
plain: Show P(n^n + 1) / n tends to infinity.
math: Prove $P(n^n+1)/n\to\infty$.

title: Growth rate of square-sum Hamiltonian cycles
plain: Find the exponential growth rate of the number of ways to arrange 1 to N in a circle with neighbours summing to squares.
math: Determine $\lim_N\frac{\log H(N)}{N\log N}$ where $H(N)$ counts Hamiltonian cycles of $S_N$, and prove the limit exists.

title: Primes on circles centred at the origin
plain: Find the largest number of prime points (p, q) lying on a single circle centred at the origin with radius up to R.
math: Determine the order of $\max_{n\le R^2}\#\{(p,q)\in\mathbb{P}^2:p^2+q^2=n\}$.

title: Thue–Morse of P(n) and P(n+1)
plain: Show the Thue–Morse values at P(n) and P(n+1) are uncorrelated.

title: Two large factors and one small
plain: Add P(n), P(n+1) and the smallest prime factor of n + 2. Tested starts reach 14, 33, or loops through 10, 42, 67, 97 or 3307. Prove these seven are the only fates.

title: The 2n+3 map
plain: Map n to P(2n + 3) + P(n). Orbits can climb past seven million before falling, yet every tested start ends in loops through 6, 9 or 50. Prove all do.

title: Peak height of the 2n+3 map
plain: For n ↦ P(2n+3) + P(n), show the highest point an orbit reaches is at most a fixed power of its start.
math: Prove there is $A$ with $\max_k f^{k}(n)\le n^{A}$ for all $n\ge3$, $f(n)=P(2n+3)+P(n)$.

title: Largest-factor tribonacci
plain: Repeatedly add the largest prime factors of the last three terms. Show the sequence is always eventually periodic.
math: For $a_{n+3}=P(a_{n+2})+P(a_{n+1})+P(a_n)$, prove eventual periodicity for every start in $\mathbb{N}_{\ge2}^3$.

title: Largest prime factor of Markov numbers
plain: Show the largest prime factor of Markov numbers tends to infinity.
math: Prove $P(m)\to\infty$ as $m$ runs through Markov numbers.

title: Seven-free Markov numbers
plain: Show infinitely many Markov numbers have no digit 7.
math: Prove infinitely many Markov numbers $m$ satisfy $7\notin m$ (decimal).

title: Apollonian packing with prime curvatures
plain: In the integral Apollonian packing with curvatures (−1, 2, 2, 3), show every large prime is the largest prime factor of some circle's curvature.
math: For the $(-1,2,2,3)$ Apollonian packing with curvature multiset $\mathcal{K}$, prove $\{P(k):k\in\mathcal{K}\}$ contains all sufficiently large primes.

title: Apollonian seven-free curvatures
plain: In the Apollonian packing (−1, 2, 2, 3), show infinitely many circles have curvature with no digit 7, and count them.
math: Prove $\#\{k\le X:k\in\mathcal{K},7\notin k\}=X^{\log_{10}9+o(1)}$ for the $(-1,2,2,3)$ packing.

title: Largest factor of p² + p + 1 small
plain: Show infinitely many primes p have P(p² + p + 1) < p.
math: Prove $\#\{p\le x:P(p^2+p+1)<p\}\gg\pi(x)$.

title: Consecutive largest factors both 3 mod 4
plain: Show P(n) and P(n+1) are both 3 mod 4 for a quarter of all n.
math: Prove $\#\{n\le x:P(n)\equiv P(n+1)\equiv3\ (4)\}\sim x/4$.

title: Largest-factor Collatz for all n
plain: Prove every start reaches a loop under the largest-factor Collatz map.
math: Prove every orbit of $f(n)=n/2$ (even), $P(3n+1)$ (odd) is eventually periodic.

title: Smallest-factor Collatz for all n
plain: Prove every start reaches 1 under the smallest-odd-factor Collatz map.
math: Prove $g^k(n)=1$ for some $k$, for every $n\ge1$.

title: 5n+1 largest-factor convergence
plain: Prove every orbit of the 5n+1 largest-factor map ends in a loop.
math: For $f_5(n)=n/2$ (even), $P(5n+1)$ (odd), prove every orbit is eventually periodic.

title: Prime Nim closed form
plain: Find an exact rule for the Prime Nim losing positions that works for every pile size.
math: Give a closed-form characterization of $\{n: G(n)=0\}$ in Prime Nim checkable in $O(\log n)$ arithmetic operations, with proof.

title: Cube-sum Hamiltonian cycles
plain: Arrange 1 to N in a circle so neighbours add to perfect cubes, for all large N.
math: Prove $C_N$ is Hamiltonian for all sufficiently large $N$.

title: Gerver constant is transcendental
plain: Show the area of Gerver's sofa is not a root of any polynomial with integer coefficients.
math: Prove $\mu_G\approx2.2195$ is transcendental.

title: Hat Ising critical temperature
plain: Find the exact critical temperature for magnets on a hat tiling.
math: Compute $\beta_c$ of the Ising model on the hat adjacency graph in closed form.

title: Hat dimer heights
plain: Random pairings of neighbouring hat tiles have a "height" landscape. Show it looks like the standard random surface at large scales.
math: Prove the height function of uniform dimer covers of growing hat patches converges to a multiple of the Gaussian free field, and compute the multiple.

title: Three colors for cube sums
plain: Can the positive integers be 3-colored so no two numbers of the same color add to a cube? Settle it.
math: Decide whether $\chi(C_\infty)\le3$, where $a\sim b$ iff $a+b$ is a perfect cube.

title: Two colors for square sums, avoiding triangles
plain: Show every way to 2-color 1 to N, for large N, makes three same-colored numbers whose pairwise sums are all squares.
math: Prove for large $N$ every 2-coloring of $[N]$ has a monochromatic triangle in $S_N$.

title: Keller maps are invertible over Q in dimension 3, degree ≤ 4
plain: Show no Jacobian-conjecture counterexample exists in 3D up to degree 4 with rational coefficients.
math: Prove every Keller map $F\in\mathbb{Q}[x,y,z]^3$ with $\deg F\le4$ is invertible.

title: Real-rank hyperoperation uniqueness
plain: Prove there is exactly one natural way to fill in the operations between addition, multiplication and powers.
math: Prove uniqueness of an analytic family $a[s]b$ on $s\in[1,3]$ under the recursion law plus a log-convexity condition in $s$, and existence.

title: Hat ground state
plain: Find the arrangement of hat tiles that minimises a natural energy, and show it is the aperiodic tiling.
math: Prove the hat tiling is the unique (up to isometry) ground state of a finite-range two-body potential on hat-shaped particles in the plane.

title: Spectre is a quasicrystal ground state
plain: Find a finite-range pair potential whose only zero-temperature arrangement is the spectre tiling.
math: Construct a finite-range rotation-invariant pair potential for which every ground state is a spectre tiling, and prove it.

title: Sofa beyond Gerver in 3 dimensions of turning
plain: A 2D hallway that turns 90° twice in a row (an S-bend): find the best sofa.
math: Determine the optimal sofa for the width-1 corridor with two consecutive right turns in opposite directions, separated by length $L$, for every $L>0$.

title: Optimal sofa is not algebraic anywhere
plain: Show the optimal sofa for a 60° turn has an outline that no polynomial equation describes.
math: Prove the boundary of the optimal sofa for the $60^\circ$ corridor contains no arc of any algebraic curve.

title: Delayed fire on the grid
plain: If the fire only spreads every other turn, find the smallest per-turn budget that always contains it.
math: Find the infimum of average firefighter budgets that contain the half-speed fire on $\mathbb{Z}^2$.

title: 3-pile shuffle mixing constant
plain: Find the exact cutoff constant for riffle-style 3-pile shuffles, in closed form.
math: For random 3-pile shuffles on $3n$ cards, prove cutoff at $c\log n$ with $c$ in closed form and window $O(1)$.

title: Prime necklaces for all n
plain: Arrange 1 to 2n in a circle so every two neighbours sum to a prime, and so do every two numbers three apart.
math: Prove for all large $n$ a cyclic arrangement of $[2n]$ with $\pi_i+\pi_{i+1}$ and $\pi_i+\pi_{i+3}$ prime for all $i$.

title: Packing hats
plain: Find the densest way to pack hat shapes when they are not allowed to tile.
math: Determine the maximal packing density of translates and rotations of the hat with reflections forbidden.

title: Kissing number of the spectre
plain: How many spectres can touch one central spectre without overlapping?
math: Determine the kissing number of the spectre polygon under rigid motions (reflections allowed).

title: Graceful trees up to 50 vertices in Lean
plain: Give a computer-checked proof that every tree with up to 50 vertices is graceful.
math: Formalize in Lean 4 that all trees on $\le50$ vertices admit graceful labelings.

title: Yang–Mills on hats
plain: Lattice gauge theory placed on a hat tiling should still have a mass gap at strong coupling and at weak coupling.
math: Prove the $SU(2)$ lattice gauge theory on the 3D product of the hat complex and $\mathbb{Z}$ has a mass gap for all couplings.

title: Squared squares with consecutive primes
plain: Find a perfect squared square whose square sides are consecutive primes.
math: Find or rule out a perfect squared square whose component sides are $p_k,p_{k+1},\dots,p_{k+r}$ for some $k,r$.

title: Spectral gap of the spectre
plain: Find the exact gaps in the energy levels of an electron moving on a spectre tiling.
math: Prove the spectrum of the adjacency operator on the spectre tiling has gaps labelled by an explicit $K$-theory group, with every label open.

title: Prime Nim with two piles
plain: Give an exact rule for who wins two-pile Prime Nim (remove a prime from one pile).
math: Characterize $\{(a,b): G(a)\oplus G(b)=0\}$ via a formula for the Grundy function $G$ of Prime Nim.

title: Integer Keller collisions
plain: Show any Jacobian-conjecture counterexample must send two different integer points to the same place.
math: Prove every non-invertible Keller map in $\mathbb{Z}[x_1,\dots,x_n]^n$ is non-injective on $\mathbb{Z}^n$.

title: Polykite growth is irrational
plain: Show the growth rate of polykite counts is an irrational number.
math: Prove $\lambda=\lim k_n^{1/n}$ for polykites is irrational.

title: Hat corona limit shape is not polygonal
plain: Show the limiting shape of hat layers has a fractal outline.
math: Prove the limit shape of scaled hat coronas has boundary of Hausdorff dimension $>1$.

title: LF-Collatz stopping time distribution
plain: Find the exact distribution of how long the largest-factor Collatz map takes to settle.
math: Prove $T_f(n)/\log n$ converges in distribution on $[1,x]$ and identify the limit law.

title: SOF Collatz with 5n + 1
plain: Use the smallest odd factor of 5n + 1 instead of 3n + 1. Show every start ends in a loop.
math: Prove every orbit of $n\mapsto n/2$ (even), $\mathrm{spf}_{\text{odd}}(5n+1)$ (odd) is eventually periodic.

title: Three of four
plain: Show infinitely often at least three of the four doubled-twin numbers are prime at once.
math: Prove there are infinitely many $n$ such that at least three of $n,n+2,2n+1,2n+3$ are prime.

title: Seven-free Carmichael numbers
plain: Show infinitely many Carmichael numbers have no digit 7.
math: Prove there are infinitely many Carmichael numbers with no digit 7 in base 10.

title: Prime Nim with prime-power moves
plain: Allow subtracting any prime power. Find exactly which piles lose.
math: Characterize the P-positions of the subtraction game with move set $\{p^k: p\text{ prime},k\ge1\}$.

title: Sofa through a revolving corridor
plain: The hallway itself slowly rotates while you push the sofa. Find the largest sofa that still makes it.
math: For the width-1 L-corridor rotating at angular speed $\omega$ relative to a sofa moving at unit speed, find the optimal area as a function of $\omega$.

title: Squared rectangles with prime sides
plain: Find the smallest perfect squared rectangle whose squares all have prime side lengths.
math: Determine the minimal order of a perfect squared rectangle with every component side prime.

title: Firefighter on the hat tiling
plain: Find the exact average number of firefighters per turn needed to contain any fire on a hat tiling.
math: Determine $\inf\{f: f\text{ firefighters per turn (averaged) contain every finite fire on the hat graph}\}$.

title: Spectre Rupert
plain: Extrude a spectre into a prism. Can a copy pass through a hole in itself?
math: Decide whether the right prism over the spectre of height 1 has the Rupert property.

title: Keller maps in dimension 3 of degree 5
plain: Show no Jacobian-conjecture counterexample exists in 3D with degree exactly 5 and rational coefficients.
math: Prove every Keller map $F\in\mathbb{Q}[x,y,z]^3$ with $\deg F=5$ is invertible.

title: Three-pile shuffle orders equal
plain: Show the three-pile shuffle and the two-pile shuffle on the same deck size have equal order infinitely often.
math: Prove $\operatorname{ord}(\sigma^{(3)}_{6n})=\operatorname{ord}(\sigma^{(2)}_{6n})$ for infinitely many $n$.

title: Hyperbolic Hex
plain: On a board tiled by heptagons in hyperbolic space, find an explicit first-player win for Hex-like connection.
math: On the $(7,3)$ tiling with a disk of radius $r$ split into four boundary arcs, give an explicit winning strategy for the first player for all $r$.

title: Few loops for square-plus-one
plain: The square-plus-one map has a loop: 89 goes to 233 and back. Show there are only finitely many loops.
math: Prove $Q(n)=P(n^2+1)$ has finitely many periodic orbits (one is $89\leftrightarrow233$).

title: The 4p+1 funnel
plain: Map a prime p to the largest prime factor of 4p + 1. Every prime tested falls into one loop of eight primes. Prove all do.
math: Prove every orbit of $p\mapsto P(4p+1)$ on primes enters the cycle $5\to7\to29\to13\to53\to71\to19\to11\to5$.

title: Three loops for 2p+3
plain: Under p ↦ largest prime factor of 2p + 3, every tested prime ends in one of three loops. Prove there are no others.
math: Prove every orbit of $p\mapsto P(2p+3)$ on primes enters one of the cycles $\{3\}$, $\{5,13,29,61\}$, $\{43,89,181,73,149\}$.

title: Spectre self-avoiding walks
plain: Find the exponential growth rate of non-self-intersecting walks on the spectre tiling, and show it is the same for every spectre tiling.
math: Prove the connective constant $\mu$ of the spectre adjacency graph exists, is the same for all spectre tilings, and is not algebraic of degree $\le2$.

title: Strict convexity of hat first-passage
plain: Give each hat-tile edge an independent random length. Prove the limiting ball of first-passage distances is strictly convex.
math: For i.i.d. continuous edge weights with finite exponential moment on the hat adjacency graph, prove the first-passage limit shape exists and is strictly convex.

title: Sandpile identity on hats
plain: The abelian sandpile on a large hat-tiled region has an identity element that looks like a fractal picture. Show it has a scaling limit.
math: Prove the sandpile identity on hat-tiled $L$-balls, rescaled by $L$, converges weakly (as a height-density measure) and that the limit is not rotationally invariant.

title: Hat Laplacian eigenvalue is transcendental
plain: Show the lowest vibration frequency of a hat-shaped drum with clamped edges is transcendental.
math: Prove the first Dirichlet eigenvalue $\lambda_1$ of the hat polygon (unit kite side) is transcendental.

title: Hearing the hat
plain: Show no other polygon has exactly the same vibration frequencies as the hat.
math: Prove the hat polygon is Dirichlet-spectrally determined among all simply connected polygons.

title: Affine prime maps all settle
plain: Fix whole numbers a and b. Send a prime p to the largest prime factor of ap + b. Every case tested falls into a loop. Prove this always happens.
math: Prove that for all fixed integers $a\ge2$, $b\ge1$, every orbit of $p\mapsto P(ap+b)$ on primes is eventually periodic.

title: The 7p+4 dozen
plain: Under p ↦ largest prime factor of 7p + 4, every tested prime ends in one loop of length 12. Prove all do.
math: Prove every orbit of $p\mapsto P(7p+4)$ on primes enters a single cycle of length 12, and identify it.

title: Longest increasing run of prime gaps
plain: Among the first N prime gaps, find the longest subsequence that strictly increases. Show it grows like a power of N and find the power.
math: Let $L(N)$ be the length of the longest strictly increasing subsequence of $(p_{n+1}-p_n)_{n\le N}$. Prove $L(N)=N^{\theta+o(1)}$ and determine $\theta$.

title: Undecidable prime-factor maps
plain: Show no algorithm can decide, given a and b, whether every orbit of n ↦ n/2 (even) or the largest prime factor of an + b (odd) eventually loops.
math: Prove $\{(a,b)\in\mathbb{N}^2:$ every orbit of $n\mapsto n/2$ ($n$ even), $P(an+b)$ ($n$ odd) is eventually periodic$\}$ is not recursive, or prove it is.

title: Digit-restricted Chowla
plain: Show μ(n)μ(n+1) has no bias on numbers n where neither n nor n+1 contains the digit 7.
math: Prove $\sum_{n\le x,\ 7\notin n,\ 7\notin n+1}\mu(n)\mu(n+1)=o(x^{\log9/\log10})$.

title: Minimal degree of a Jacobian counterexample
plain: The 2026 counterexamples have degree 7. Find the smallest degree any 3D counterexample can have.
math: Determine $\min\{\deg F: F:\mathbb{C}^3\to\mathbb{C}^3$ non-invertible Keller map$\}$.

title: Square-plus-one orbits rarely loop
plain: Show almost every starting number's square-plus-one sequence never repeats.
math: Prove the set of $n$ whose orbit under $Q(n)=P(n^2+1)$ is eventually periodic has natural density 0.

title: Square-sum chains in primes
plain: Show there are arbitrarily long chains of primes where neighbours sum to squares.
math: Prove for every $k$ there are primes $p_1,\dots,p_k$ with $p_i+p_{i+1}$ a perfect square for all $i<k$.

title: Gerver sofa algebraic independence of its angles
plain: Gerver's sofa is built from two special angles. Show they are algebraically independent over the rationals.
math: Prove the two transcendental switching angles $\varphi\approx0.0392$ and $\theta\approx0.6813$ in Gerver's construction are algebraically independent over $\mathbb{Q}$.

title: Square-plus-one orbit mod 3
plain: Show the square-plus-one sequence starting at 2 lands on primes of both kinds mod 3 infinitely often.
math: Prove $Q^k(2)\equiv1\pmod 3$ and $Q^k(2)\equiv2\pmod 3$ each hold for infinitely many $k$.

title: Seven-free Friedlander–Iwaniec primes
plain: Show infinitely many primes of the form x² + y⁴ have no digit 7.
math: Prove infinitely many primes $x^2+y^4$ free of the decimal digit 7.

title: The 3p+4 seven-cycle
plain: Send a prime p to the largest prime factor of 3p + 4. Every prime tested ends in the loop 11 → 37 → 23 → 73 → 223 → 673 → 17 → 11. Prove all do.
math: Prove every orbit of $p\mapsto P(3p+4)$ on primes enters the cycle $(11,37,23,73,223,673,17)$.

title: The 5p+4 nine-cycle
plain: For p ↦ largest prime factor of 5p + 4, every tested prime ends in one loop of nine primes through 11. Prove all do.
math: Prove every orbit of $p\mapsto P(5p+4)$ on primes enters the cycle $(11,59,23,17,89,449,173,79,19)$.

title: Escaping p²+p+1
plain: Start at 2 and repeatedly take the largest prime factor of p² + p + 1. Show the sequence grows without bound.
math: Prove the orbit of $2$ under $p\mapsto P(p^2+p+1)$ is unbounded.

title: Exponential growth of square-plus-one orbits
plain: Show square-plus-one sequences, when they don't loop, grow at a steady exponential rate in the number of digits.
math: Prove that for almost every $n$ (density 1), $\lim_{k}\frac1k\log\log Q^k(n)$ exists and equals a constant $\gamma>0$; identify $\gamma$.

title: Hat percolation is conformally invariant
plain: Show critical percolation on the hat tiling's tiles has crossing probabilities given by Cardy's formula.
math: For critical site percolation on hat tiles, prove crossing probabilities of conformal rectangles converge to Cardy's formula as the mesh $\to0$.

title: Critical Ising on the hat is SLE(3)
plain: Show the interface in the critical Ising model on a hat tiling converges to the random curve SLE(3), even though the graph is not isoradial.
math: For the critical Ising model on the hat graph with Dobrushin boundary conditions, prove the interface converges to chordal SLE$_3$.

title: Hat packing density is irrational
plain: The densest packing of hats without reflections leaves gaps. Show the best density is an irrational number.
math: Prove the maximal packing density of congruent hats under orientation-preserving isometries is irrational.

title: Hat Neumann eigenvalue is transcendental
plain: Show the first nonzero frequency of an insulated hat-shaped membrane is transcendental.
math: Prove the first nonzero Neumann eigenvalue $\mu_2$ of the hat polygon (unit kite side) is transcendental.

title: Critical hat Ising temperature is irrational
plain: Show the critical temperature of the Ising model on a hat tiling is not a rational multiple of the coupling.
math: Prove $\beta_c J\notin\mathbb{Q}$ for the ferromagnetic Ising model on the hat graph.

title: Square-sum Ramsey with many colours
plain: Colour 1 to N with r colours. Show some colour contains four numbers whose six pairwise sums are all squares, once N is large enough.
math: Prove that for every $r$ there is $N$ such that every $r$-colouring of $[N]$ has a monochromatic $K_4$ in $S_N$, or show it fails for some $r$.

title: Hat Hofstadter gaps all open
plain: Show every gap predicted by the gap-labelling theorem actually opens in the hat tiling's electronic spectrum.
math: Prove the dry ten-Martini property for the vertex adjacency operator of the hat tiling: every gap label in the $K_0$-group of the hull corresponds to an open gap.

title: Gerver sofa eigenvalue is transcendental
plain: Show the lowest vibration frequency of a drum shaped like Gerver's sofa is transcendental.
math: Prove the first Dirichlet eigenvalue of Gerver's sofa is transcendental.

title: Spectre drum eigenvalue is transcendental
plain: Show the lowest frequency of a drum shaped like the curved spectre tile is transcendental.
math: Prove the first Dirichlet eigenvalue of the spectre domain is transcendental.

title: Is eventual periodicity of square-plus-one decidable?
plain: Is there an algorithm that decides, for any n, whether its square-plus-one sequence eventually loops?
math: Decide whether $\{n: (Q^k(n))_k \text{ is eventually periodic}\}$ is recursive, where $Q(n)=P(n^2+1)$.

title: Conformal radius of Gerver's sofa
plain: Map a disc conformally onto Gerver's sofa, sending the centre to the sofa's centroid. Show the scale factor is transcendental.
math: Prove the conformal radius of Gerver's sofa at its centroid is transcendental.

title: An irrational sum over largest factors
plain: Add 1/(n·P(n)) over all n ≥ 2. Show the total is irrational.
math: Prove $\sum_{n\ge2}\frac{1}{n\,P(n)}$ is irrational.

title: Bounded orbits for polynomial prime maps
plain: Given a polynomial f, can an algorithm decide whether the orbit of 2 under n ↦ P(f(n)) stays bounded?
math: Prove or disprove: $\{f\in\mathbb{Z}[x]:\text{the orbit of }2\text{ under }n\mapsto P(|f(n)|)\text{ is bounded}\}$ is decidable.

title: Infinite cube-sum paths
plain: Colour the integers with two colours. Show there is an infinite one-coloured chain where neighbours sum to cubes.
math: Prove every 2-colouring of $\mathbb{N}$ admits $a_1<a_2<\cdots$ of one colour with $a_i+a_{i+1}$ a perfect cube for all $i$.

title: Self-avoiding walk on the hat tiling scaling
plain: Show long self-avoiding walks on the hat tiling spread out like distance n^{3/4}, the same as on the square grid.
math: Prove $\mathbb{E}|\omega_n|^2=n^{3/2+o(1)}$ for uniform $n$-step SAWs on the hat-tiling edge graph.

title: Continued fraction of the P-constant
plain: Show the constant formed by largest prime factors as continued fraction digits is transcendental.
math: Prove $[0;P(2),P(3),P(4),\dots]$ is transcendental.

title: Undecidability of Prime Nim variants
plain: Show there is no algorithm that takes a polynomial f and decides whether the subtraction game with moves {f(p) : p prime} has eventually periodic Grundy values.
math: Prove $\{f\in\mathbb{Z}[x]:\text{Grundy sequence of the game with move set }f(\mathbb{P})\cap\mathbb{N}\text{ is eventually periodic}\}$ is undecidable, or decidable.

title: SOF Collatz is undecidable in general
plain: Show some natural family of smallest-factor Collatz maps has an undecidable reach-1 question.
math: Prove the problem "given $a,b$, does every orbit of $n\mapsto n/2$ or $\mathrm{spf}(an+b)$ reach 1?" is undecidable.

title: Gerver constant is normal
plain: Show the digits of Gerver's sofa area appear with equal frequency in base 10.
math: Prove $\mu_G$ is normal in base 10.

title: Sofa for every corridor
plain: Give one method that finds the best sofa for every hallway shape.
math: Prove optimal sofas for piecewise-linear corridors are characterized by a finite system of ODEs on boundary arcs, and solve it in closed form for all right-angle corridors of width ratio $r$.

title: Prime Nim is periodic in base 2
plain: Show the Grundy values of Prime Nim follow a pattern that a finite machine reads off the binary digits, or prove none exists.
math: Decide whether the Grundy function of Prime Nim is $2$-automatic.

title: Hyperoperation at rank 2.5 is transcendental
plain: Show 2 combined with 3 at "rank 2.5" in the natural hyperoperation family is transcendental.
math: For the unique natural family $a[s]b$, prove $2[2.5]3$ is transcendental.

title: Square-sum chromatic number
plain: Find exactly how many colors the infinite square-sum graph needs.
math: Determine $\chi(S_\infty)$ exactly.

title: Cube-sum independence
plain: Find the largest set of numbers up to N where no two add to a cube.
math: Determine $\alpha(C_N)$ asymptotically, with second-order term.

title: Keller maps classification
plain: List every Jacobian-conjecture counterexample in 3D, up to symmetry.
math: Classify all non-invertible Keller maps $\mathbb{C}^3\to\mathbb{C}^3$ up to composition with polynomial automorphisms.

title: Hat aperiodicity in Lean, minimal
plain: Give a computer-checked proof that the hat tiles only aperiodically, in under 2000 lines.
math: Produce a Lean 4 proof of the hat's aperiodicity of at most 2000 lines using only Mathlib.

title: Spectre gap labelling
plain: Show every allowed energy gap of the spectre tiling actually opens.
math: Prove the dry ten-Martini property for the adjacency operator on the spectre tiling.

title: Chess on the hat board
plain: Solve a chess-like game on a hat-tiled board with 10 pieces per side.
math: Weakly solve the game with standard chess move semantics translated to the hat graph on a fixed 64-tile patch.

title: Toroidal Go 9×9
plain: Who wins Go on a 9×9 board that wraps around in both directions?
math: Weakly solve Go on $\mathbb{Z}_9^2$ with area scoring and komi $0$.

title: 7×7 Othello
plain: Who wins Othello on an odd 7×7 board with a fixed off-centre start?
math: Strongly solve Othello on a $7\times7$ board from the standard initial cross shifted to the corner-adjacent center.

title: Hat random walk return
plain: Find the exact probability that a random walk on hat tiles returns to its start within n steps, asymptotically.
math: Prove $p_{2n}(o,o)\sim c/n$ on the hat graph and compute $c$ exactly.

title: Firefighter on Z³
plain: How many firefighters per turn are needed to contain a fire in 3D, as a precise growth rate?
math: Determine $\lim_{t\to\infty}f(t)/t$ for the minimal firefighters needed to contain fire on $\mathbb{Z}^3$ by time $t$.

title: Sudoku count asymptotics
plain: Count n²×n² Sudoku grids exactly, to leading order.
math: Prove $\#\text{Sudoku}(n)=\left(\frac{(n^2)!^{2}}{n^{2n^2}e^{\dots}}\right)\!(1+o(1))$ with an explicit leading term.

title: Polykite complete classification
plain: For every polykite, decide whether it tiles, and if so how.
math: Give an algorithm deciding, for any single polykite, whether it tiles the plane, and prove it correct.

title: Gerver sofa is not periodic in its digits
plain: Show the digits of Gerver's sofa area never fall into a repeating pattern in any base, and are not "too well" approximable.
math: Prove the irrationality measure of $\mu_G$ equals 2.

title: Hat Ising free energy
plain: Find the exact free energy of magnets on a hat tiling at the critical point.
math: Compute $f(\beta_c)$ for the Ising model on the hat graph in closed form.

title: Spectre dimers are critical
plain: Show random pairings of spectre tiles have long-range correlations, like the square grid.
math: Prove dimer correlations on the spectre tiling decay as a power law with exponent 2.

title: Origami with a bounded number of layers
plain: Find the best origami base for any tree when no point may have more than 4 layers of paper.
math: Give an algorithm for the minimal square paper for uniaxial bases of metric trees with layer count at most 4, with proof of optimality.

title: Seven-free primes have a bounded gap
plain: Show infinitely many pairs of seven-free primes lie within a fixed distance of each other.
math: Prove $\liminf(q_{n+1}-q_n)<\infty$ where $q_n$ enumerates the 7-free primes.

title: Square-plus-one merging
plain: Many square-plus-one sequences run into the one starting at 2. Decide whether every sequence eventually does, apart from those caught in loops.
math: Decide whether every $n\ge2$ whose $Q$-orbit is not eventually periodic satisfies $Q^a(n)=Q^b(2)$ for some $a,b$.

title: Partition numbers contain a 7
plain: Show that from some point on, every partition number has a 7 among its digits.
math: Prove there is $N$ such that the decimal expansion of $p(n)$ contains the digit 7 for all $n\ge N$.

title: Hat-tiling site percolation is irrational
plain: The critical probability for percolation on the hat tiling is about 0.5442. Prove it is irrational.
math: Prove $p_c^{\mathrm{site}}$ of the hat-tiling dual graph is irrational.

title: Gerver sofa and the circle
plain: Show the area of Gerver's sofa is not a rational combination of π and 1.
math: Prove $\mu_G\notin\mathbb{Q}+\mathbb{Q}\pi$.

title: Irrationality of the hat percolation threshold, bond
plain: The bond-percolation threshold on the hat tiling's edges is about 0.7982. Prove it is irrational.
math: Prove $p_c^{\mathrm{bond}}$ for the hat tiling's edge graph is irrational.

title: Gerver's constant is not a period
plain: Show the area of Gerver's sofa cannot be written as an integral of an algebraic function over an algebraic region.
math: Prove $\mu_G\approx2.2195$ is not a Kontsevich–Zagier period.

title: Irrational orbit sum
plain: Add the reciprocals of the square-plus-one sequence starting from 2. Show the total is irrational.
math: Prove $\sum_{k\ge0}1/Q^k(2)$ converges and is irrational.

title: Hat SAW connective constant is irrational
plain: Show the growth constant of self-avoiding walks on the hat tiling's neighbour graph is irrational.
math: Prove the connective constant of the hat adjacency graph is irrational.

title: Unforced blow-up near the forced one
plain: Show the known forced Navier–Stokes blow-up can be made to work with forcing that decays to zero at the blow-up time.
math: Prove there exist smooth $u_0$ and $f\in L^1_tL^2_x\cap C^\infty$ with $\|f(t)\|_{L^2}\to0$ as $t\to T^-$ such that the forced 3D NS solution blows up at $T$.

title: Prime Nim complexity
plain: Decide exactly how hard it is to tell if a Prime Nim pile is losing: show it can't be done fast without unproven assumptions.
math: Prove, unconditionally, that deciding $G(n)=0$ in Prime Nim requires time $(\log n)^{\omega(1)}$.

title: LF-Collatz loops classified forever
plain: Show every largest-factor Collatz-type map for every odd multiplier has only finitely many loops, with a uniform recipe.
math: For every odd $a\ge3$, prove $f_a(n)=n/2$ (even), $P(an+1)$ (odd) has finitely many cycles, with an explicit bound in $a$.

title: Hyperoperation transcendence
plain: Show values of the natural hyperoperation at non-integer ranks are algebraically independent.
math: Prove $\{2[s]3: s\in\mathbb{Q}\cap(2,3)\}$ is algebraically independent over $\mathbb{Q}$.

title: Square-sum Ramsey numbers
plain: Find the exact point at which every 2-coloring of 1 to N contains a same-colored square-sum clique of size 4.
math: Determine $\min\{N: \text{every 2-coloring of }[N]\text{ has a monochromatic }K_4\text{ in }S_N\}$, or prove none exists.

title: Optimal 3D origami
plain: For every 3D shape, find the smallest sheet of paper that folds into it.
math: Give a characterization, with an algorithm, of the minimal-area square that folds into any given polyhedral surface.

title: Prime Nim Grundy values are unbounded in density
plain: Show each Grundy value of Prime Nim appears with a precise positive density, and compute them all.
math: Prove $d_k=\lim\frac1x\#\{n\le x: G(n)=k\}$ exists for every $k$ and give a formula.

title: Lorenz dimension is irrational
plain: Show the Hausdorff dimension of the classic Lorenz attractor is irrational.
math: For $\sigma=10,\beta=8/3,\rho=28$, prove $\dim_H(\mathcal{A})\notin\mathbb{Q}$.
